  keyboard for the palette's whole life, so that typing never has to be resumed, and the list cannot take it: a
  reader that follows the keyboard heard the typed letters and nothing of the rows the arrow keys moved through,
  though each row's name was set. The palette now says the row the selection reaches - "3 of 12:" and the row's
  name, which is what it is and where it lives - as the arrow keys, Page Up and Down, Home and End move it and as
  typing changes the results, and the empty-results sentence when nothing matched, as a notification that replaces
  the last one rather than queueing every row passed (`Services/ScreenReaderNotice`); the search box's help text is
  the footer's key legend as a sentence, "Up and down arrows to move, Enter to open, Escape to close".
  `PaletteAnnouncementTests` holds the position, which counts the rows that can be chosen and not the section
  captions, the sentence and the wiring.

- **Fixed: the administrator roles page's two lists had no names, no titles, and rows a screen reader called by a
  class name.** Neither grid had an accessible name, the two cards no title - only the column headers told the roles
  from who holds one - and neither row class said anything of itself, so a reader announced each row as
  "hMailServer.ControlPanel.Views.RolesView+RoleRow". The cards are titled Roles and Who holds a role, the grids are
  named the same, and a row says its role and what it is for, or the account, its role and its domains
  (`Services/RowSpeech`). `RowSpeechTests` holds the sentences and the page.

- **Fixed: rows on the code-built list pages were announced by their class name or as unlabelled values.** A screen
  reader read a row of the audit trail as "hMailServer.ControlPanel.Views.AuditTrailView+RowView", and so the rows of
  the suppression list and its bounce counts, the message trace, journaling, eDiscovery's cases and their lines, the
  domain white and black list, setting profiles, the never-ban list, the message-store consistency list, the app
  passwords and the Active Directory picker; a collection page's row was its first three raw values with no column -
  "Yes, zen.spamhaus.org, 127.0.0.2", the first a tick box's. Each row now says itself as one statement: its cells
  that have something in them, a bare value with its column's name - "gone@old-provider.example, Hard bounce, 5.1.1,
  Refused while delivering, Since: 2026-10-07 03:10:43, Expires: Never"; "gone@old-provider.example, Hard: 3, Soft:
  0, …"; "zen.spamhaus.org, Active: Yes, Score: 3" - a collection page's cells as the grid shows them, a choice's
  word and not its number. `RowSpeechTests` reads every page for a class bound to a list's columns and holds each to
  a ToString of its own.

- **Fixed: four facts were only in row tool tips, out of reach of the keyboard.** Why a message was held in
  quarantine, what the receiving server answered for a suppressed address ("550 5.1.1 user unknown"), an audit row's
  whole detail and whether a traced event can be followed were each on screen only while the mouse rested on the
  row. Under each of those lists the selected row's fact is now in a compact card titled with what it is - Why it was
  held, What the receiving server answered (or Note for an address put there by hand), Detail - in text that can be
  selected and copied, collapsed while nothing is selected (`Views/RowDetailStrip`); the rows keep their tool tips. The
  audit trail and the message trace lay their toolbar, notice, list and detail out as the suppression list does, so
  that the list keeps three rows in the narrowest window and the page scrolls below them, where the detail would have
  taken the list's height. `RowDetailStripTests` holds the strip, each page's fact and its place after the list.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel's page forms had no Alt keys, one action had more than one, and keys collided.** Domain,
  Address, Password, Alias address, Delivers to and the list's address on the domains page, Account, Role and Domains
  on the administrator roles page, and some fifty more field captions - on the routes, TCP/IP ports, IP ranges, rules,
  SSL certificates, incoming relays, MX query, send-out, diagnostics, journaling, Directory synchronisation, Directory
  authentication and DNS records pages and in eight dialogs - carried no key while the dialog fields around them did, so
  Alt reached a page's buttons and none of its boxes. Each carries one now, and a field whose box has a button beside
  it - the backup file, the destination folder, a DKIM key file, a route's address to add - puts the keyboard in the
  box, where its key did nothing. A verb has one key on every page: Remove is Alt+M (the route and group member
  dialogs and the two-factor panel said Alt+R) on the button and in the question it asks, whose Remove was Alt+R in
  the group members, recipients, journaling, sample domain and sandbox token questions, Browse… Alt+B, Copy Alt+C,
  Search Alt+S, Remove expired Alt+E and Restore defaults Alt+F, and Resume is Alt+E, where on the server status page
  it was Alt+R beside Refresh; the route dialog's Add is Add address. The Backup & restore page's five cards hold some
  thirty-five captions, more than there are letters, and shared eight - Alt+P was the encryption passphrase, the
  archives to keep and Put the message back, and WPF, given two targets for one key, only moves the focus between
  them: the card that holds the keyboard now answers its own keys first, and a key it does not have goes to the page
  as before (`Views/AccessKeyScope`). `build/check-mnemonics.py` reads field captions in XAML and in code, captions
  set in code on a XAML page's buttons and the buttons a confirmation names, holds a verb to one key and each card of
  such a page on its own, and holds a dialog tab's keys against the Save button under every tab, which it meant to and
  did not: in 109 places, all in translations, a tab's key was its dialog's Save - Starkes Passwort erzeugen and
  Speichern were both Alt+S on a German account's General tab. Some 170 translated captions in fifteen languages took
  another letter to make room. `--self-test`, which CI runs, proves each rule against a page made to break it;
  `AccessKeysTests` holds the pages.

- **Fixed: the dashboard's chart range did not say which range was chosen.** Live, 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days were
  four buttons that marked the chosen range by its colour alone: a screen reader heard "Show Live" and three more
  buttons with none of them chosen, and pressing the chosen range read its history from the server again. They are a
  radio group named Chart range now - the caption beside them says Chart range where it said Show - with the chosen
  range still drawn as the primary button: one tab stop, the arrow keys move the choice, a reader hears "Live, radio
  button, selected, 1 of 4", and the chosen range pressed again does nothing. The note on a history range is under the
  choice, where it ran past the window's edge. `ChartRangeGroupTests` holds the group.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel's empty lists said only that they were empty, never what that meant or how to fill
  them.** Eleven list pages shared "Nothing here yet - Add creates the first entry."; the SSL certificates, IP ranges,
  routes and TCP/IP ports pages said "No ... yet." with no button, though with no IP range the server refuses every
  connection; the REST API keys page said it twice, a card apart; and the recipient, group member and never-ban lists
  were blank boxes. Each list now says what its emptiness means, in a sentence of its own - "No block lists, so
  connecting addresses are not looked up in any.", "No IP ranges, so this server refuses every SMTP, POP3 and IMAP
  connection until one exists." - and its empty state carries the action that ends it: *Add the first entry…* on
  every list the generic editor draws, *Restore the default ranges* and *Restore the default ports*, *Add a route*
  (which puts the keyboard in the add form), *Set up ACME…* beside the certificates' form, *Create the first key…*,
  and *Add the first domain…* on the domain white and black list. The REST API keys page says it has no keys once, by
  the list. A list card whose empty state carries an action is floored at what it holds - its grid's three rows on a
  FillPanel of its own and the empty state laid over them, under the grid's column headers - so that the action is
  never cut off in a short window, where the card's fixed 157 pixels held a glyph and a sentence and nothing more, and
  the glyph is never drawn across the headers, as it was under the quarantine's; the dialogs' lists and the never-ban
  list show their empty state in the list's place, and only after a read that worked.

- **Fixed: an Add, an Edit or a Delete on a Control Panel list said nothing, and the list lost its place.** Every list
  the generic editor draws - the SURBL servers, DNS blacklists, white list, blocked senders, allow and block list,
  greylisting lists, blocked attachments, groups, remote domains, and the lists on the domain and account dialogs'
  tabs - set "Added at…", "Saved at…" or "Deleted." and then read the list again, and the read hid the notice when it
  worked, so the outcome was never seen; the read rebuilt the rows, so the edited row lost its selection, the list
  jumped to the top and a new entry was neither selected nor in view. The list is read first now and the outcome said
  after it, in the notice above the list, naming the entry - "multi.surbl.org added." - and said again when the words
  are the same as the last time; the entry added or saved is selected, scrolled into view and has the keyboard, a
  delete selects the row that took its place, an Add, an Edit or a Delete that failed keeps the row it was asked
  about, and Refresh keeps the selected entry selected.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel's Backup & restore page said what its buttons did a screen or more away from them,
  printed a restore job's raw state, and made a restore type what it could have chosen.** Restore started, a mailbox
  restore started and the schedule saved all went to one notice above the first card, and only Save settings raised a
  toast; a mailbox restore's outcome printed the server's state token ("Job 7 is running: …"), and its JSON when it
  could not be read; the whole restore asked for "the backup XML file" though a backup writes an archive
  (HMBackup YYYY-MM-DD HHMMSS.7z), the mailbox restore for an archive's name typed by hand, and the one-message restore
  for an id copied out of a monospace listing; the browse buttons opened the pickers of whichever machine the Control
  Panel ran on, the server's or not; and "No passphrase is set: the archive is not encrypted…" was an Information
  notice. Each card now says what its buttons did in its own footer, beside them, and every job started raises a
  toast; a restore job's outcome is a sentence at its level - queued and running at Information, done at Good, done
  with messages that could not be put back at Warning, failed at Critical with the server's reason - and an answer
  that cannot be read is said so. A new card lists the archives in the destination, newest first, by the server's own
  naming rule, with when each was taken (server time) and its size; choosing one fills the whole restore's path and
  the mailbox restore's archive, and the whole restore names the archive it takes. The account's messages in an
  archive are a grid to choose from, and Put the message back acts on the one chosen, from the archive and for the
  account it was listed from, and asks about it by its subject, folder and date where it asked about "message 1042";
  another archive or account named above clears the listing, and the grid says, while nothing is listed, what lists
  the messages. Connected to another machine, the archive card says it cannot list that machine's folder and the
  browse buttons are off, with a tool tip saying to type the path as the server sees it; the no-passphrase notice is
  a Warning.

- **Fixed: verifying a domain on the Control Panel's DNS records page took seven Check clicks, and Copy said nothing.**
  Each card - MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, the MTA-STS record and its policy, TLS-RPT - had its own Check and its own
  "Not checked" line, with nothing that said how the domain stood, and Copy host and Copy value put the text on the
  clipboard best effort, so nobody could tell whether a copy had worked. *Check all records*, in the page header, runs
  every check of the domain at once and sums them up in one notice above the cards, at the worst level any check
  reached, a line per verdict naming its records, worst first - "Not published: DKIM, TLS-RPT", "Published and
  correct: MX, SPF, DMARC" - while each card shows its own verdict as its Check does; a check a card already has
  running is waited for, and a check that fails is said as "Lookup failed", on its card and in the notice. Every
  copy button says *Copied* beside a tick for two seconds, and a screen reader is told; a copy that failed, another
  program holding the clipboard, is said in a toast with the reason.

- **Fixed: the Blocked attachments and greylisting lists never said whether the switch that applies them was on.** The
  Blocked attachments page showed "5 rules" and the list whether attachment blocking was on or off, so a list of
  patterns read as patterns at work while none was applied, and the virus scanning overview was the one place that
  said so; the greylisting white list and bypass list said nothing while greylisting was off. Each reads its switch
  with the list now: while attachment blocking is off a Warning above the list says that none of its patterns is
  applied (one sentence for none, one and several), and while greylisting is off an Information notice says that no
  sender is delayed, so the list changes nothing; each offers the settings page that holds the switch. The blocked
  entries are patterns throughout - the count, the column, the delete question - where the page called them wildcards
  and rules, and the subtitle says what the server does with a match, replacing the attachment with a short note
  before the message is delivered, where it said the wildcards were stripped from incoming messages.

- **Fixed: the Administrative access page's Two-factor tab never said whether either second factor was on, and turning
  the server's factor off asked for a code nothing checked.** Both cards offered "Set up or turn off …" and said the
  state only after the dialog had been opened and closed, as a line of green or red under the button, so a factor
  legitimately off read as a failure. Each card now starts with a pill and a sentence - On, or Off at Warning for the
  factor the server enforces and at Normal for this tool's own - read when the tab is built and again after the dialog
  closes, and its button says what it will do, Set up or Turn off; a state that cannot be read says Not read and the
  button waits for Reload. The server keeps the secret and has nothing that checks a code against it, so the dialog no
  longer asks for "the current 6-digit code" and accepts any six characters: it says that turning the factor off
  removes the code requirement for this tool, scripts and the REST API, its button is Turn off the second factor, and
  Enter is Close. After an enrolment the server refused there is no code box keeping the keyboard beside a Confirm
  that cannot be pressed, the box takes digits only, typed or pasted - a space typed is held off, and a code pasted as
  authenticator apps copy it, "123 456", keeps its six digits - and the recovery text names the [Security] section of
  hMailServer.ini, the editor run as administrator and the service restart, as the server's own text does.

- **Fixed: Live logs could stream the wrong file, went silent at midnight and put every problem in the grey
  subtitle.** The page took the newest file matching hmailserver_*.log, which is as often the AWStats, backup or
  events log or a per-service log as the day's, and kept it past midnight, when the server opens the next day's, while
  still saying Streaming. It now follows today's file of the log chosen in a new Log list - everything, errors, script
  events, backup and restore, and SMTP, IMAP and POP3 conversations while the server writes those apart - by the
  server's own name for it, and moves to the next day's file once the server has opened it, with a line saying where
  the log continues. The script events and backup logs are read as the UTF-16 the server writes them in on Windows,
  the other logs as UTF-8. Pause says since when and how many new lines are waiting, Clear is Clear view with a tool
  tip saying the log file is not changed, and each line is laid out as its time, type, thread, session and text
  without the file's quotes and tabs; a copy is still the line as the file has it. A log folder that is not on this
  computer, a log not written yet today and a log folder that belongs to the administrators, for a Control Panel not
  run as administrator, whether it did when the page opened it or was made theirs while the page streamed it, are each
  said in the list's place, with Logging's page where switching logging on is the cure, where each replaced the
  subtitle above an empty card; a file not there yet is shown as soon as the server writes it.

- **Fixed: the Diagnostics and MX query results were raw text in a box that looked like an input, and an old scan read
  as a green OK.** Diagnostics showed "[ OK ]" and "[FAIL]" lines in a read-only text box with an input's underline,
  which looked empty, with no summary, put "Diagnostics failed" in the same box, and kept Run enabled while running,
  so a second click ran the checks twice; the MX query wrote "Query failed" and "no mail servers" into its box as
  plain text, and both pages' Copy was enabled with nothing to copy. Each check is now a row - a Passed or Did not
  pass pill, its name, and what the server found under it - below a summary at the level of the worst ("3 of 4 checks
  passed. Failed: Outbound port 25."), a check that did not pass being Critical in its pill and in the summary alike,
  Run and Query wait while a run is in progress, with the loading state in the results' place, a failed run is a
  Critical notice, the MX answer is a summary at its level (the mail servers found, none found, or the query failed)
  above the servers it names, and Copy waits for an answer. The message-store consistency card says No problems found
  at Good only for a scan under two hours old of a check that is switched on; a scan of a check that is off is
  Information, with how old it is and a button to the Server limits & expert settings page, and one of a check that is
  on but has not scanned since is a Warning that says how old it is.

- **Fixed: Server status worked the uptime out from the Control Panel's clock, its statistics had no period, and the
  counters had other names on the Dashboard.** The uptime was the server's local start time subtracted from the clock
  of the computer the Control Panel runs on, wrong by the difference between their time zones, in units fixed as "d h
  m" in every language ("5d 3h 12m" in Japanese); the server gives no clock of its own, so the uptime is now worked
  out only where the two clocks are one, a session on the server's own computer, and says it is not known here
  otherwise, in each language's own units ("5 T. 3 Std. 12 Min.", "5 日 3 時間 12 分"), the Dashboard's tile as well; the
  start is shown in the reader's date format and marked as the server's time. The statistics are under two lines,
  Since the service started, with the time marked as the server's, and Connected now, where six figures sat side by
  side as one kind; the counters are named the same on both pages, Messages processed and Spam detected - the counter
  is every message the spam checks detected, deleted or only marked, where Server status said Spam removed and the
  Dashboard Spam blocked; and the row of the update's state is captioned Update status, where its caption was the
  verb, "Aktualisieren" in German.

- **Fixed: the folder permissions list named an entry's rights by the first word of each right's caption.** A row read
  "user00@example.com - Lookup, Read, Keep, Set, Delete, Delete", Delete folder and Delete messages both being
  "Delete", and in German the rights were "Ordner", "Nachrichten" and "Gelesen/Ungelesen-Status". Each right has a
  short name of its own, translated whole - Lookup, Read, Seen, Flags, Insert, Post, Create, Delete folder, Delete
  messages, Expunge, Administer, as the IMAP rights are named - and the entry dialog keeps the full captions.

- **Fixed: the Rules page's scope list had no visible caption, and its title and subtitle ignored the scope chosen.**
  A list reading "The server" sat between the search box and Move up with nothing to say what it chose - only a screen
  reader heard "Rules of" - and after a domain was chosen the page still said "Global rules" and "4 rule(s), evaluated
  top to bottom." The list is captioned Show rules for, its caption and list wrapping with the actions as one group,
  the page is titled Rules as the navigation map names it (Global rules stays a search alias), and the subtitle names
  whose rules it counts: "4 rules of the server, evaluated top to bottom.", "2 rules of example.com, evaluated top to
  bottom.", one whole sentence for none, one and several in each case.

- **Fixed: why a quarantined message was held was only in a hover tool tip, and nothing could search the held
  messages.** Keyboard and screen-reader users never got the reason, and the row's accessible name left it out. The
  reason of the selected message is now shown under the list and is part of the row's accessible name, which a screen
  reader says once as the selection moves; a search above the list finds held messages by sender, recipients, subject
  or reason, says when it finds none, and, where the server listed only its most recent, that it looked at those. Held
  is how long ago the message was held, in short units ("5 h ago"), where the server's clock is this computer's, and
  the reader's date and time where it is not, under the caption Held (server time), the age in words and the whole
  time in the tool tip marked as the server's, where it was the database's raw string in every language. The text
  columns share the width the grid itself has, not the window's: the HELO name has a column only where the grid is
  1000 pixels wide or more, its headers icon now beside the preview's in the subject; the sender and the subject are
  each as wide as their longest, up to a limit, wherever there is room for both - at 1280 pixels with the sidebar
  open, a session on the server's computer shows the sample's addresses and subjects whole in English, German and
  Japanese - and share what there is where there is not; the recipients keep a column where there is room for it as
  well, which in the narrowest window there is not; and Held and Score are as wide as their widest word, with room for
  the sort arrow on the column sorted by. At 1280 pixels the addresses and the HELO name were cut while Subject had
  room to spare.

- **Fixed: the spam filtering overview's structure was flat, its scores unlabelled, and it left out the external
  filtering engine.** The card titles and the two phase headings were one size and weight, with no heading level on
  the cards; each row ended in an unlabelled "2", "per entry" or "-"; every row's link read "Settings…" and the lists
  card's "Open…" sat some 600 pixels from its label; and with an external engine attached (rspamd, FilterHookUrl) the
  list of checks left it out, so the overview could state a highest total of 12 that the engine's own score made
  false. The cards are level-2 headings and the phases small strong overlines under them at level 3, over a header
  row - Spam check, State, Adds - in which a score reads "+2", "the entry's score" or "adds nothing"; each link names
  the page it opens, and a list's name is its link with its count beside it; the external filtering engine is the
  eleventh check, after SpamAssassin, adding the engine's score or the reject score, so that with it on the total is
  open-ended and the size limit's note names it among the checks that need the body; and the subtitle reads "Each spam
  check in the order the server runs it, what it adds to the score, and what the total does to a message."

- **Fixed: a field's caption was the quietest text of its row, and a field's message did not mark the field and sat
  under its hint.** A caption above a box was 12-pixel secondary text over a 12-pixel hint four points of alpha
  lighter, so that "Void SPF lookups allowed before permerror (0 = no limit)" could not be told from the paragraph
  under it, while a check box's caption on the same card was 14-pixel primary text. A field's message - "A domain is
  required." - appeared under the hint, as much as 50 pixels from its box, which kept its neutral border and the
  violet focus ring, and the dialog grew by the message and moved Add and Cancel from under the pointer. A caption is
  body text now, 14 pixels in the primary colour, and the hint stays small and tertiary; the message sits directly
  under the box, the box's border turns the danger colour and its focus ring with it, and an edit of the value takes
  the message away; every dialog whose field can be refused - Allow or block a domain, the never-ban name, the
  suppression list's Add, both two-factor setups, the administrator password, a REST API key's Create, the port
  binding, the mailbox move, a rule's criterion and an incoming relay's Edit among them - keeps room for its message,
  so that its buttons stay where they were, while a row shown or collapsed still grows or shrinks the dialog.

- **Fixed: the Domains & accounts page's four forms answered a bad value with a message box or with nothing at all.**
  Add domain said "Enter a valid domain name." in a message box, Create account said "Address and password are
  required." in one that named neither box, and Add alias and Add list did nothing with an empty box. Each refusal is
  said under the box at fault now, with the keyboard put in it and every empty box marked on one press: "Enter a
  domain name such as example.com.", "Enter the account's address.", "Enter a password, or press Generate.", "Enter
  the alias address.", "Enter where the alias delivers." and "Enter the list's address."; the messages go with the
  next press, an edit of the box, a password put in by Generate, the domain changed or the page opened again, and a
  message box is left for the server's own refusal. Each form's button stays beside its box when a message appears
  under it.

- **Fixed: SSL certificates, IP ranges and Directory authentication (LDAP) refused a value in a message box or a
  notice that pointed at no box, and IP ranges put 15 in place of a priority that was no number.** "Name, certificate
  file and private key file are required." and "Name, lower IP and upper IP are required." were message boxes; a
  priority of "high" became 15 without a word; the ends of a range went to the server as typed; LDAP's port and
  timeout were refused only in the notice under the header; and the certificate form's note sent the reader to "the
  box below" for a box beside the others. Each value refused is said under its box now, with the keyboard put in the
  first and every box at fault marked on one press: an empty name or file, the lower and upper address of a range as
  the server reads an address ("Enter the lower address of the range, such as 10.0.0.0."), the upper of the same kind
  as the lower and not below it, a priority that is a whole number ("Enter a whole number."), and on the LDAP page
  the port and the timeout on their boxes as well as in the notice. The certificate's note names the Key passphrase
  box. On both pages' Add forms the boxes and Add line up whatever a caption wraps to, and a message under one box
  moves none of the others.

- **Fixed: the Routes, TCP/IP ports, Rules, Incoming relays and Server sendout forms refused a value in a message
  box, and some put in or sent on what was typed.** "Domain and target host are required.", "Enter a valid port
  number.", "Enter a name for the new rule.", "Name, lower IP and upper IP are required." and "From address and
  subject are required." were message boxes that took the keyboard from the form; a route's port of "25a" became 25
  and its host went unchecked, a port's bind address went to the server as typed, and the relays page sent "abc" to
  "xyz" as a range. Each value refused is said under its box now, every box at fault on one press, with the keyboard
  in the first: a route's domain, its host (a name such as smtp.partner.com or an IP address) and its port from 1 to
  65535; a port's bind address and number; a rule's name; a relay's name and the lower and upper address of its
  range, of one kind, the upper not below the lower; and the sendout's sender address, subject and message. On each
  Add form the boxes and the button line up whatever a caption wraps to, and a message under one box moves none of
  the others.

- **Fixed: the Add and Edit dialog of every list page closed before the server was asked, so that a refused save lost
  everything typed.** The dialog behind SURBL servers, DNS block lists, the exemption lists, blocked senders, blocked
  attachments, remote domains and the rest closed on Add or Save, and the page then wrote the entry and reported a
  refusal in a message box, "Could not save: ...", with what was typed gone; the quarantine's digest settings did the
  same. The dialog writes with itself open now, and a refusal is said under the field it names - or under the first
  field - with every value kept, so that the entry can be put right and saved again; the digest settings hold the
  link's hours to the server's 1 to 720 before they write anything, and put the address back where the server refuses
  the hours after taking it, so that a refusal followed by Cancel leaves both as they were. Every field's caption has
  an Alt key, assigned so that none is another's or a button's, in Japanese and Chinese as "(_D)" after the caption;
  a number box is as wide as a number, where it stretched to 412 pixels for a score; Blocked senders' Score is a
  number box holding 100, where it was a text box, and its address is required, each with a sentence under it saying
  what it does. The dialog keeps room for its messages, so that Add and Cancel stay where they are.

- **Fixed: the distribution list dialog sent a number that was no number as -1, and said a refused save where it
  could not be seen.** "Keep archived messages for" and "Digest hour (0-23)" were text boxes whose text, when it was
  no number, went to the server as -1 for it to refuse, and the refusal appeared at the top of a body that had been
  scrolled to the archive fields, so that Save seemed to do nothing; an emptied List address kept the old one without
  a word, and a new one renamed the list without saying so. The address and the two numbers are checked on their
  fields before anything is written - "Enter a number of days from 0 (for ever) to 3650.", "Enter an hour from 0 to
  23.", the ranges the server takes - with the field scrolled into view and the keyboard in it; a refusal of the
  server is brought into view; and List address says under it that changing it renames the list and keeps its members
  and settings. In every dialog a field refused below the fold is now scrolled to with its message.

- **Fixed: a folder permission's account or group was checked only after its entry dialog had closed, and its eleven
  rights had to be ticked one by one.** Save closed the access-control entry, the folder's permissions then looked
  the name up and, finding none, said "No account found with address '...'" in their own notice with the entry typed
  gone; the account or group was free text with nothing to pick from; and the IMAP rights were offered raw, in one
  column. The entry resolves its account or group before it closes now, and says an empty box or a name the server
  has none of under the box, with the entry kept; the box lists the server's accounts or groups to pick from, and
  fills in as the first letters are typed; Read only, Read and write and Full control tick their rights in one press
  (read only is Lookup, Read messages and Keep seen/unseen state; read and write adds Set flags, Insert, Delete
  messages and Expunge, but not Post or the rights over the folder itself), and the rights are in two columns.

- **Fixed: a rule's criterion was saved with no header name or no value, and the message size and the delivery attempt
  opened on "contains" with no unit.** The criterion dialog wrote a custom header with no name, which matches nothing,
  and an empty value, which "contains" finds in every message and "does not contain" in none. It now says "Enter a
  header name." or "Enter a value." on the field and saves nothing, an empty value being kept only for "equals" and
  "does not equal", which ask whether the field is empty. Message size and Delivery attempts open on "is greater
  than", offer the four comparisons a number has, are captioned Value (bytes) and Value (attempts) over a line that
  says what the number counts - the whole message, attachments included, and 1 on the first delivery attempt - and
  take a whole number, stored as the number, since "equals" compares the text: "03" is stored as 3, which "Delivery
  attempts equals 03" then matches. A criterion saved with another comparison keeps it. The IF and THEN dialogs name
  the rule under their heading: "Add a criterion to the rule “Invoices”.", "An action of the rule “Invoices”.".

- **Fixed: with no domain selected, the Domains page's account form kept the last domain's address and the alias and
  list forms stayed live.** On an empty server, or with the selected domain gone, the accounts card was titled "Select
  a domain" with nothing under it and its Address box still read user@ the last domain, and Add alias and Add list did
  nothing when pressed. With no domain the account form is empty and disabled, the card says "Select a domain to see
  its accounts." as the alias and list cards say theirs, and the alias and list forms are disabled until a domain is
  selected - also after a read that found no domain to select, where no selection change put the cards in that state.

- **Fixed: Create account on the Domains page took a weak password without a word.** The account dialog judges a
  password as it is typed and asks before it saves a weak one; the page wrote whatever was typed, so the first mailbox
  a new administrator made skipped the check. The page now shows the dialog's verdict under the password as it is
  typed - "Weak password - add 12+ characters, ...", "Fair password ...", "Strong password." - in the level's colour,
  on a line of its own above the buttons where they wrap, and asks "Create the account with this weak password
  anyway?" before it creates an account with a weak one, Cancel the answer Enter gives.

- **Fixed: Directory authentication saved an incomplete configuration switched on without a question.** With "Use
  LDAP directory authentication" ticked and the host name or the search base empty, Save wrote the section, which the
  server reads within two seconds and then tries no directory sign-in at all, directory-linked accounts going on
  through Windows logon, which works only on a computer joined to the domain - though the card at the top of the page
  said what was missing. Save now asks first, naming the empty fields by their captions and saying what happens
  meanwhile, with Save anyway and Cancel, Cancel the answer Enter gives; a section saved switched off is filled in at
  leisure, as before.

- **Fixed: Directory synchronisation's Preview and Apply ran the saved selection while the editors above showed
  unsaved changes.** A run reads the [LDAP] section as saved, so a preview pressed after the search filter was changed
  and not saved showed the old filter, and Apply then applied it. While the search filter, the three attributes or the
  maximum entries differ from what was read or saved, Preview and Apply are disabled and the run card says so at its
  top, with Save and preview, which saves the selection and then previews it - and previews nothing when the save is
  refused. A preview within two and a half seconds of a save on either directory page - Save and preview's own, or
  Preview pressed just after Save - waits, the card saying "Reading the directory...", until the server has read what
  was saved, which it does two seconds after it last looked: it previewed the selection before the save, and Apply was
  then enabled for the new one. The schedule, which a run does not read, does not count.

- **Fixed: the hMailServer.ini settings pages wrote whatever was typed into a number, the MTA-STS policy mode was free
  text and the DNS override took anything.** The ports, timeouts, cache lifetimes, sizes and work factors on Transport
  security, Certificates (ACME), API & monitoring, Server limits & expert settings, Authentication and Web services &
  autoconfiguration were 520-pixel text boxes, and Save wrote a port of 70000 or a PBKDF2 work factor the server then
  reports and replaces with its own. Each is a 180-pixel box, as on the other settings pages, that keeps the number as
  typed, and Save holds it to the range the server reads it in - a port from 0 to 65,535, the OpenTelemetry interval
  from 5 to 3600, the MTA-STS max age from a day to a year, a work factor 0 or its range - saying "Enter a whole number
  from 0 to 65,535." on the field and writing nothing on the page. A number is digits, or digits grouped as the reader
  writes them - 10,000 in English, 10.000 in German, 10 000 in French - and anything else is refused the same way,
  never rounded, read as another number or put back to the value before: "1.5", "1,5" in English, "30s". The MTA-STS
  policy mode is a list of enforce, testing and none, each saying what it does; the DNS override is held to one IPv4
  address as the server reads it; addresses are 260 pixels wide and other text the width of the form, as on Directory
  authentication and Directory synchronisation, whose boxes were 320 to 620 pixels and whose numbers are now 180. The
  drop size for oversized inbound messages is captioned in KB, the unit the server compares it in, where it said bytes.

- **Fixed: fields that count only while their switch is on stayed editable while it was off.** A domain's account,
  alias and list limits, its plus-addressing character, signature, relay credential, out-of-office text for local
  senders, subject tag, disclaimer, key rotation interval, digest hour and webhook subjects; an account's forward
  address, auto-reply, signature and Windows account; a route's credential; an IP range's expiry; the ACME and OAuth2
  settings under their master switches; and the anti-virus notices, which are sent only when the whole message is
  deleted, all stayed live under a switch that was off. Each now follows its switch, dimmed with its caption and hint
  while it is off and saved as it stands, except that a value there the server would not take - a port of 0 under
  ACME switched off - is not held against the save, since the field cannot be reached to correct it, and is kept as
  the server has it; the fields the server reads for something else stay live - a domain's out-of-office subject and
  text, which answer outside senders in an account's place under the override, the two signature boxes that hold back
  every signature, and the rotation's period, retention and key size, which Rotate now uses. An IP range's expiry is a
  date and a time of day on one line, where it was one box of "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS", each said on the field when it
  is missing or not a time.

- **Fixed: the sentence for a failure that blocks every read started in lower case and named a button the page did
  not have.** The lost link, the unreachable database and a session that is not the server administrator's were
  written to follow "Could not ...:", so a page that said one alone - Setting profiles, the quarantine, the audit
  trail, message trace, an account's app passwords and second factor - read "Critical the connection to the
  hMailServer service was lost ...", and each told the reader to press Reload, beside a button called Refresh or none
  at all. Each is now a whole sentence that begins with a capital and names no button - "The connection to the
  hMailServer service was lost - it was most likely restarted. The Control Panel reconnects by itself; try again in a
  moment.", "... then try again.", "Sign in with the hMailServer server-administrator account to view or change these
  settings." - as are the two for an older server and for an answer this Control Panel could not read, in all
  seventeen languages; after what failed it follows a colon, as the server's own refusals do, where the setup
  checklist, the Dashboard and the Active Directory check put it after a dash. A reinitialise that does not report
  Running within thirty seconds names the Server status page, where it named a Status page, and a passphrase saved
  for a certificate deleted in the meantime says that it was deleted after the list was read, where it said "reload
  the page".

- **Fixed: the Control Panel named settings by their hMailServer.ini keys, and twice by the server's source code,
  where the reader sees a caption on a page.** The setup checklist said "Set TlsRptFromAddress in the [Settings]
  section of hMailServer.ini", "ACME is enabled but AcmeDomains is empty", "Neither OAuth2Issuer nor OAuth2Audience is
  set", "DisableAUTHList names it" and "ProtectStoredSecretsWithDPAPI is 0", the never-ban list "list the address in
  AutoBanNeverBan", DNS records "NOTE: MtaStsHostingEnabled=0, so the server will NOT serve this policy at all", the
  Dashboard "MetricsHistoryDays is 0 in hMailServer.ini", Diagnosing stalled mail named its nine timeouts by key, the
  Backup & restore hints began "hMailServer.ini setting BackupVerifyRestore" and said "so BackupMessagesDBOnly can
  only be changed on the server itself", and two notes ended "(Utilities::ComputerName)" and "(the table lives in
  WindowsEventLog.h)". Each now names the setting by its caption and its page - "Set 'TLS report sender address' on
  the Transport security page", "add the address to 'Never auto-ban these addresses' on the Auto-ban page", "Note:
  'Serve MTA-STS policies for local domains' is off on the Web services & autoconfiguration page", "it is listed in
  'Do not offer AUTH on these local TCP ports' on the Authentication page", "Message finalization deadline (240)" - in
  all seventeen languages, each with the caption and the page title its own catalogue gives them. A key stays only
  where nothing on screen captions the setting - where hMailServer.ini is the one place to set it ([Directories]
  DataFolder and LogFolder, and AdministratorTotpSecret, deleted by hand when the authenticator is lost) - and on the
  Directory authentication (LDAP) page, whose captions carry their keys; a test holds every text to it against the
  keys of the settings pages and of the settings search, acronyms in them included. The update check's caption lost
  its "(UpdateCheckEnabled)", the event log's last level is "Every error the server reports" where it was "Everything
  ErrorManager reports", and the directory authentication page's port is captioned Port, where it read "Port (Port)".

- **Fixed: the SSL certificates page said a failed read with the reason alone and no way to read the list again.** It
  now leads with "Could not read the certificates:", as the other list pages do, with Try again beside it, the list
  emptied and Add disabled until a read works.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel sent the reader to pages that do not exist and named options by words that are not their
  captions.** The backup warnings pointed at "the backup log on the Logs page", the update settings at "the Status
  page", the sender-authentication headers and ARC trust at "the Anti-spam page, under sender authentication", the
  setup checklist at "the Backup page" and "the Anti-virus page's Sandbox tab", the Windows directory tab at "the
  Directory authentication page", and the null sender card said allowed and blocked domains "have a page of their own
  under Anti-spam", a group the sidebar does not have; the account's spam overrides needed "Add reason to header"
  switched on, the distribution list's hint explained "Anyone in the domain", the blocked-recipients claim "Refuse"
  and "Deliver and record", and the status page said "No public host name is configured in the SMTP settings". Each
  now names the page by its title - Live logs, Server status, Anti-spam settings (and its Sender auth tab), Backup &
  restore, Anti-virus settings, Directory authentication (LDAP), "the Allowed and blocked domains page, under Spam &
  virus filtering" - and the option by its caption: 'Add X-hMailServer-Reason header', 'Anyone in the domain can
  send', 'Refuse it, with the reason', 'Deliver it, and only record it', and "No host name is set: 'Host name
  (HELO/EHLO greeting)' on the Protocols page's SMTP tab is empty", in all seventeen languages with each catalogue's
  own titles and captions. build/check-catalogues.py now also reads the English: every "the X page" it names must end
  in a title the navigation map gives, and what it says something is under must be a page or a group of the
  navigation.

- **Fixed: the account dialog's Windows directory tab sent the reader to "the password on the Account tab", and the
  directory authentication page to "the account's Directory tab"; neither tab exists.** They are the General and
  Windows directory tabs, and the directory page now names the checkbox and the box to fill in there by their
  captions - 'Check this password against Windows (Active Directory, or a local Windows account)' and 'Windows user
  name' - where it said "the Active Directory option" and "the AD user name", in all seventeen languages.
  build/check-catalogues.py holds every "the X tab", "its X tab" and "the page's X tab" in the English to a tab
  header a view declares.

- **Fixed: the Anti-spam settings and Anti-virus settings pages' hints were essays - the void SPF lookups hint ran to
  137 words, the rsa-sha1 one to 122 and the DMARC tree walk one to 127, with RFC and project history and asides such
  as "The operator who asked for it uses 20.", and the scanner-failure card said its default three times.** Every hint
  on the two pages now says what the setting does and what its safe value or its consequence is, in two sentences at
  most - "How many terms of a sender's SPF policy (a:, mx:, exists:) may find no DNS record before the result is
  permerror. RFC 7208 sets 2; 0 removes the limit." - and the default of the scanner-failure choice is stated once, in
  the option "Deliver it (default)". The reasons the hints lost are in the pages' help topics: a new section of
  docs/SmtpPolicy.md, "The reasons behind the Anti-spam settings page", and "When a scanner cannot run" under "The
  virus scanner" in docs/SealedMail.md, where the help opens for the Anti-virus settings page. In all seventeen
  languages.

- **Fixed: the account and domain dialogs phrased the same things differently.** The account dialog's "Last l_ogon" is
  "Last sign-in", in the reader's short date and time with "(server time)" where it was the server's date as the
  machine's culture wrote it - and Never for the date the server keeps when there is none, which it showed as 30
  December 1899; "Zero-access mailbox" reads Off or On, with what that means under it, where the explanation was the
  value; neither read-only row carries an Alt key any more; and a Windows domain account on an unjoined server "can
  never sign in". The domain's signature choices are "Use only when the account has no signature", "Replace the
  account's signature" and "Append to the account's signature"; its relay password is "leave empty to keep current" as
  the account's is; DKIM's rows are spelt canonicalisation; and every range in the three dialogs says what 0 means one
  way - "(MB; 0 = no limit)", "(days; 0 = for ever)", "(days; 0 = once per absence)". In all seventeen languages.
  build/check-mnemonics.py holds a read-only row's caption (DialogFields.ReadOnlyField) to carrying no key, in English
  and in every catalogue.

- **Fixed: nothing in the Control Panel went back to the page the administrator came from.** Opening a page
  replaced the one on screen and recorded nothing, so after following one of the links between pages - the
  Dashboard's attention list, the setup checklist's buttons, an overview's rows, the stalled-mail steps, a Related
  link, a palette result - the only way back was to find the page again in the sidebar or the palette. The
  breadcrumb bar now starts with Back and Forward, each naming the page it opens in its tool tip ("Back to Delivery
  queue (Alt+Left)") and its accessible name, and neither pressable when there is nothing that way; Alt+Left and
  Alt+Right, the keyboard's own Back and Forward keys and the mouse's two side buttons do the same, and the
  palette's Keyboard shortcuts list names them. The history holds the pages opened since sign-in, fifty at most,
  each with where it was scrolled and the tab it was on, so that Back returns to the place as well as to the page; a
  step asks about unsaved changes as every way to another page does, and Stay leaves the page and the history as
  they were.

- **Fixed: a jump to a page left its sidebar row on the sidebar's bottom edge and the rest of its group hidden.** The
  palette, the Welcome tiles, the Related links, the pages' own buttons and the tours ended with the row's
  BringIntoView, which scrolls as little as it can: at 1280 by 800, Discovery stopped at the foot of the sidebar with
  API & monitoring and REST API keys under the fold, Spam exemptions with eight rows of its group hidden, and Anti-spam
  settings reached by search with eleven. Once the jump is laid out the sidebar now shows the page's whole group -
  moving as little as shows it all, its heading kept on screen, and not at all when the group is already on screen -
  and, in a window too short for the group, puts the page's row a third of the way down; Welcome, the Dashboard and
  About, which have no group, are brought into view as before.

- **Fixed: only three Related links were drawn beside the breadcrumb, so deliberate pairs were dropped and twelve
  pages were reached by none.** The bar drew the first three entries of a page's list whatever the room: the queue
  never offered Diagnosing stalled mail, LDAP never Directory synchronisation, the greylisting exemptions never the
  bypass list, SSL/TLS never Auto-ban and the block lists never IP ranges; Anti-spam settings did not link the
  quarantine, nor Logging the message trace or the audit trail; and Administrator roles, Remote domains, Server
  messages, Server sendout, Webmail, the Allow and block list, the Greylisting bypass list, Allowed and blocked
  domains, Directory synchronisation, Diagnosing stalled mail, the Suppression list and Discovery were the link of no
  page. The bar now draws as many as fit beside the trail, in the order listed, again as the window is resized, with
  the rest in a More (n) drop-down - Related pages (n) where not even the first fits - and each list begins with its
  partners (Anti-spam settings: Spam filtering overview, Quarantine, DNS block lists; Logging: Live logs, Message
  trace, Audit trail; SSL/TLS: Transport encryption overview, Transport security, Auto-ban). Every page but Welcome and
  About is now the Related link of another, and each pair the navigation map puts side by side lists the other among
  its first three, which a test holds.

- **Fixed: a domain administrator was offered Related links to pages the role cannot open, and pressing one did
  nothing.** The Domains page linked Public folders, Groups and Rules, which need the server administrator and which
  the sidebar hides from that role; the breadcrumb drew them from the navigation map without asking, and opening a
  page the role's tree leaves out found no row and returned without a word - from a Related link, a palette result,
  a Welcome tile or a tour step alike. The Related links are now only the pages the signed-in role may open, by the
  same rule the sidebar is built by - a domain administrator's two pages, Domains and the Suppression list, lead to
  each other - and a jump to a page the role cannot open says so: "Your role cannot open Rules."

- **Fixed: F1 opened a document about something else on some twenty pages, and the help ignored the page's tab.**
  Each page was mapped to "the nearest" document: Domains opened the domain's tagging and disclaimer, Groups and
  Public folders what a backup carries, IP ranges country blocking, the five certificate and TLS pages one remote
  domain's outbound TLS, LDAP the webmail's OpenID Connect and Directory synchronisation the people directory, Web
  services the calendar, Server sendout the distribution lists, the block lists this server's own reputation watch,
  SURBL, the spam overview and the anti-spam settings the SMTP policy, the spam exemptions the allow and block
  list, the virus pages what an encrypted message gets, Server limits the service account, and the Logging page's
  four tabs all the syslog document. Two documents are new - Domains and accounts (adding a domain, an account, an
  alias and a list, what a switched-off domain or account still does, and every tab of the domain's and the
  account's dialogs) and Public folders and groups (folders and sub-folders, the access-control list and its eleven
  rights, groups and their members) - and the pages open a document about themselves: the certificates and ACME the
  certificate a new installation makes, the transport encryption overview what it starts with, the greylisting
  exemptions what greylisting does, Server limits the settings that bound each stage, Administrative access how the
  administrator password is kept. A page no document covers yet says so beside its title and purpose, over the list
  of every document, rather than open one about something else. A tab with a document of its own opens it while it
  is the tab showing - Logging's SNMP, Audit trail and Alerts & webhooks, the anti-spam settings' Sender auth, Host
  checks, Greylisting and Spam traps, the anti-virus settings' Sandbox, Auto-ban's Countries and Compromised accounts,
  Performance's Message store, Advanced's Scripting and Migrations, Delivery of e-mail's Feedback, Reputation and
  Mailing lists, and four of the Webmail page's - and the help follows the tab as it changes. The pane opens each
  document at its top, or at the page's heading once the document has been laid out, where it kept the place of the
  document shown before and reached the heading only on a document already showing; and two documents whose prose
  wraps to put "0." at the start of a line - Service account and Source packages - no longer stop the pane, which read
  the line as a list numbered from 0 and could not draw it. build/check-help-map.py holds every tab entry to a tab its
  page builds, and fails a document listed as reference-only whose title or name meets a tab's or a card's heading -
  the significant words of one among the other's - unless the document that page opens links it or the checker says
  why it is about something else, so that the documents of Server limits' Windows service account card and of the
  Feedback tab's Reports your domains receive card are linked from the stalled-mail document and the complaints
  document those pages open.

- **Fixed: Control Panel pages were headed with other names than the sidebar and the breadcrumb gave them.** The
  breadcrumb read Anti-spam settings over a page titled "Anti-spam", Anti-virus settings over "Anti-virus", Domains
  over "Domains & accounts", Certificates (ACME) over "Automatic certificates (ACME)" and Web services &
  autoconfiguration over "Web services & client autoconfiguration", cut to "autoconfigu..." at 760 pixels with its
  pill pushed under it; and the Domains page's subtitle spoke of "mailboxes" over a page of accounts. A page now names
  its navigation key in its header (`PageHeader.PageKey`), which takes the page's title from the navigation map, so the
  sidebar, the breadcrumb, the Ctrl+K palette, the help pane and the page say one name. Where a page and its entry had
  said two, the clearer is the title and the other a search alias: "Certificates (ACME)" is now "Automatic
  certificates (ACME)" in the sidebar as well, and the old title and its documented path still find the page. A page
  with nothing more to say than its navigation description shows that description as its subtitle, in the same
  words, where the DNS block lists, spam exemptions, greylisting exemptions, routes, MX query and server sendout pages
  said it again in others; and the Domains page reads "The domains this server hosts, with their accounts, aliases and
  distribution lists." `PageTitlesTests` holds every page MainWindow builds to naming its key, and no page header to a
  title of its own (review findings F215, F025 and F080).

- **New: an Updates page in the Control Panel.** Check for updates, Download update and Install update were on Server
  status, under a row of its Server card, and the policy that drives them - the daily check, the channel, the
  download, the unattended window, the signature checks - was a card on API & monitoring; About showed the version but
  not whether a newer one was waiting, and nothing was called Updates or Upgrade, so Ctrl+K "update" found only
  setting rows, ranked last. The Updates page, under Maintenance beside Backup & restore, holds the version this
  server runs, the update check's verdict and the three steps above the policy, which is the same card under the title
  "How this server updates"; its help is UpdateFeed.md, and the palette finds it by Update, Upgrade, New version, Live
  update, Patch, Release channel and Automatic updates, and by the tasks "install a new version", "turn on automatic
  updates" and "is there a new version". A read of the update status that fails says why on the card, with Try again,
  and holds Check for updates, Download update and Install update until a read works, as Server status held them; with
  the link to the service lost the page says so once, under its header, and the card's readouts say Not read. The card
  sits under the page's notice and the line that says where its settings are kept, as on every settings page. Server
  status, the Dashboard and About say in one line when a release is waiting - "hMailServer 6.3.7 is available." - with
  Open Updates beside it, shown to a credential that may open the page, and the same line says, as Server status's
  update row did, an update step that failed and the last apply's outcome - "Last update: rolled-back 6.3.7: ..." at
  Warning, an apply that went as asked at Information - until the Updates page has shown the outcome to that reader;
  the Control Panel that opens again after an administrator's install says how it ended on the Updates page, and "Not
  checked yet" points at the daily check below it rather than at API & monitoring. API & monitoring names the page
  under On other pages (review finding F272).

- **Fixed: settings filed under pages whose names do not describe them could not be found from those pages' names, and
  two aliases sent the reader to the wrong page.** Logging holds the alerts, outbound webhooks and SNMP; API &
  monitoring the Windows Event Log, the ManageSieve listener and the graceful shutdown, while its Webhooks alias
  outranked the real webhook settings and the Sieve alias sent the reader to the Rules page; Auto-ban holds the
  countries and the compromised accounts, Advanced the IPv6 delivery, the disk space, the migrations and the PST
  import, and Server limits & expert settings the PROXY protocol, XCLIENT, the per-account sending limits and the
  event-script timeout, none of which their descriptions or aliases named; and Delivery of e-mail's Rules tab sat one
  sidebar row from the Rules page with neither linking the other. Each page's description, which is its tool tip in
  the sidebar and its line in the Ctrl+K palette, now names what it holds, and its aliases find it: Webhooks, Alerts
  and SNMP open Logging, Sieve and ManageSieve open API & monitoring, Countries, GeoIP and Compromised accounts open
  Auto-ban, PST import and Migrations open Advanced, PROXY protocol and XCLIENT open Server limits & expert settings.
  The palette has the tasks "block mail from a country", "import a pst file", "send an alert to another system" and
  "put a proxy in front of the server". Delivery of e-mail's Rules tab says that it limits what every rule may do and
  opens the Rules page, the Rules page and Delivery of e-mail signpost each other among the three related pages the
  breadcrumb bar shows, and Incoming relays signposts Server limits & expert settings. The cards themselves stay where
  they are: moving them to the pages named for them is the owner's to decide with the new groups (review finding
  F273).

- **Fixed: a setting found by the Control Panel's Ctrl+K palette opened its page on the first tab, with nothing
  marked.** The settings index carried a setting's label, key and page and nothing of where on the page it was, so
  "MaxMind country database" opened Auto-ban on its Auto-ban tab, three tabs from the setting, and its row said only
  "Opens Sign-in & access > Auto-ban". The index now records each setting's tab and card
  (`build/generate-settings-index.ps1`), the row says "Sign-in & access > Auto-ban > Countries" - the tab on a page of
  tabs, the card on a page of one scroll - and the page it opens shows the setting: the settings pages choose its tab,
  scroll its row a third of the way down the page, with room for the ring and the start of what follows it (a row
  already in view with that room stays where it is), put the keyboard in its editor and draw a ring round the row in
  the focus colour, once, fading unless Windows has animations turned off and in the system highlight under High
  Contrast. A row that shares its key with others on its page is shown by its label: Auto-ban's four country rows, one
  for each kind of connection, open at IMAP, POP3 or the web as chosen, not all at SMTP (review finding F274).

- **New: the spam filtering overview says which list to use, and checks a sender against every list.** Eight lists
  decide whether a sender is let through or stopped, and two of them can do either - the spam exemptions, the allowed
  and blocked domains, the blocked senders, the DNS block lists, the greylisting exemptions, the greylisting bypass
  list, SURBL and the allow and block list - and each page explained at most one neighbour, with nothing to say
  whether a sender was on any of them. The overview's "The lists behind the checks" is now "Which list do I need?":
  one row for each list, in the order a message meets them, with when the server reads it, what it is matched against
  and what a match does, its page and its count. Under it, "Check a sender" takes an address, a connecting IP address
  or both and says what each list does with them - stops it, lets it through, adds to the score, depends on a
  condition (an IP range, an SPF, DKIM or DMARC pass), no match, not checked, or not reached - by the rules the server
  matches each list by: the exemptions' IP ranges and address wildcards, an entry with an @ as one exact address and
  one without as a domain with its subdomains, the most specific entry of the allow and block list and a block on a
  tie, an expired entry skipped, the greylisting exemptions' wildcards, and an exact domain over a .suffix. The
  answers are the server's, in the order it reads the lists: a spam exemption that covers the sender keeps the server
  from every other list but the allow and block list, which delivery still reads; a blocked domain is refused at MAIL
  FROM, before any later list; and an allowed domain is never greylisted, nor refused or quarantined by its score, so
  a blocked sender's entry adds to the score without stopping it. Above the rows, a line says which list decides, at
  its level and with its sentence - "The list that decides is Allowed and blocked domains. The entry mass-mail.example
  blocks this domain: its mail is refused at MAIL FROM." - or that none does and the spam checks and their score
  decide, and a screen reader hears it once the check is done, the keyboard staying in the address box. The DNS block
  lists and SURBL are asked of the network as mail arrives and are not checked here, nor are entries matched against
  the HELO name alone; a list that cannot be read says so while the others answer, and the line then says the answer
  may change (review finding F269).

- **Fixed: the Authentication page opened on fifteen OAuth2 fields, live while OAuth2 was off, and Ctrl+K sent
  two-factor and SASL searches to it.** Password storage and SMTP AUTH - what every server uses - were below the fold,
  and "Two-factor", "SASL", "CRAM-MD5" and "APOP" opened a page with none of them, while "2FA", "TOTP" and the mailbox
  password policy on Administrative access found nothing. The cards are now Password storage, SMTP authentication,
  Sign-in to the webmail and the Control Deck, and OAuth2 last (the owner's decision of 9 October 2026); the OAuth2
  fields are greyed while Accept OAuth2 bearer tokens is unticked, as a note under it says, and follow it as it is
  ticked. The second factor's names - Two-factor, 2FA, TOTP, One-time code - and the mailbox password rules' -
  Password policy, Password expiry, Password history, Breached passwords - open Administrative access, whose subtitle
  and description now say that it holds the administrator's password and second factor and the rules every mailbox
  password is held to, every one of its policy cards': length and characters, common and breached passwords, reuse and
  expiry; SASL, AUTH PLAIN, AUTH LOGIN, CRAM-MD5 and APOP open Protocols, where the mechanisms this server offers are
  switched; and Authentication's Related links begin with Protocols, Directory authentication (LDAP) and
  Administrative access.

- **Fixed: Transport security's subtitle said "Outbound mail authentication and encryption policies." over cards about
  inbound mail, and the page was one scroll of ten cards, six of them mail authentication, with Save scrolling away.**
  The page has four tabs - Encryption (DANE and DNSSEC, MTA-STS), Signing (ARC sealing and inbound filtering, DKIM
  signature timestamps and oversigning, the Authentication-Results header), Forwarding (SRS and BATV) and Reports
  (TLS-RPT and DMARC) - drawn as the other tabbed settings pages are, the header with Reload and Save changes above
  the strip and each tab scrolling under it, and a Reload or a return to the page stays on the tab it was on. The
  subtitle and the page's description read "Encryption to other servers, the signatures this server adds and checks,
  the results it records, forwarded mail and the reports it sends." - the checks are Signing's on inbound mail, the
  refusal of DKIM signatures whose expiry has passed and the filtering of ARC chains; SRS, Sender Rewriting Scheme,
  BATV, DKIM oversigning, DKIM expiry, Authentication-Results, Received-SPF and DMARC reports find the page in Ctrl+K.
  The ARC inbound filtering card, which only said that it is configured on Anti-spam, has a row with Open… that opens
  Anti-spam settings on its Sender auth tab, where the trusted sealers are, and Server limits & expert settings' row
  for SRS and BATV opens the Forwarding tab: a signpost row that names a tab opens its page on it
  (MainWindow.NavigateToTab). So does every other way in that knows where its subject is, where each opened the page
  on Encryption: the setup checklist's ARC sealing item, and the Dashboard's link to it, open Signing and its TLS
  reporting item Reports; Ctrl+K's "stop forwarded mail failing spf" and "reject forged bounce messages" open
  Forwarding; and a Ctrl+K search that finds the page by one of its aliases opens the tab that holds it - SRS and BATV
  on Forwarding, ARC, DKIM oversigning and Authentication-Results on Signing, DMARC reports and TLS-RPT on Reports -
  while its title, or a word such as "TLS" that two tabs' aliases begin with, opens it as it is. The checklist's items
  for the host name, the administrator's second factor, ARC inbound filtering and the attachment sandbox open the tabs
  their texts name too: Protocols' SMTP, Administrative access' Two-factor, Anti-spam settings' Sender auth and
  Anti-virus settings' Sandbox. Only the header and the strip are pinned, as on the other tabbed settings pages: the
  notice and the line that names where the settings are kept are above the first card of the tab on screen and scroll
  with it, and in a window under 600 pixels of page the subtitle is the title's tool tip - at 760 by 520 the pinned
  lines left the cards some 140 pixels, and 40 with the notice of a page read from hMailServer.ini.

- **Fixed: the Welcome page's "Or browse by area" tiles were not the sidebar's areas.** Six tiles were written into the
  page: "Domains & accounts" beside the group Accounts & domains, opening a page the tree calls Domains; "Server
  settings", promising protocols, delivery, anti-spam, anti-virus and advanced options and opening Protocols alone;
  the Dashboard, the next row of the sidebar; and Transport security, an expert page. The tiles are now the groups of
  the tree the signed-in credential sees, in the sidebar's order, each with the group's glyph, title and purpose, and
  each opening the group's first page - so a renamed or reordered group renames or moves its tile, and a role whose
  tree leaves a group out has no tile for it (a domain administrator sees Accounts & domains and Monitoring &
  troubleshooting). A tile's tool tip, and what a screen reader hears after its name, say which page it opens; the
  tiles of a row are as tall as each other and each row as tall as its tallest tile.

- **Fixed: Diagnosing stalled mail's "Test SpamAssassin and ClamAV" opened a page that tests neither, and its rows of
  links were cut in a narrow window.** The link went to Diagnostics, which runs port 25, MX, backup-folder and IP
  checks; it is now two, Anti-spam settings: test SpamAssassin and Anti-virus settings: test ClamAV, each opening its
  page on the tab with the scanner's test (SpamAssassin, ClamAV), and the ClamAV timeouts link opens the ClamAV tab
  too. Every row of buttons wraps, where the row of three timeout links (708 pixels in English, about 790 in German
  and Japanese) and the German debug-logging row were cut at 760 pixels; the page is the form's width, 760 pixels,
  where each step's paragraph ran to about 180 characters a line; and that paragraph is body text at the top of the
  step's card, where it was the card's description in 12-pixel caption text above tables and bullets of 14.

- **Fixed: the texts that send the reader to the Control Deck had no button and no address, and called it three
  names.** A case is opened there, alert rules and webhook subscriptions are set there, trap addresses declared, held
  messages reviewed, migration jobs started and a room's booking policy set there, and a list's members' delivery is
  shown there, and only the REST API's card said what it is. An Open the Control Deck button now stands beside them -
  in Discovery's header; as the first row of the Spam traps, Compromised accounts, Alerts, Outbound webhooks and
  Migrations cards, and on the REST API's card; under the notes of the account dialog's Identity tab, the domain
  dialog's Reports received and Webhooks tabs and the distribution list's list manager; and under the setup
  checklist's attachment sandbox finding - and opens the REST listener's root, where the Deck is served, in the
  browser; its tool tip and its accessible help text give the address. A text that sends the reader to the Deck on the
  server itself, which a Control Panel on another machine cannot open, may have none: a settings tab's notice for a
  REST API that listens on the server alone. While the Deck cannot be opened from here the button is disabled and says
  why, beside it on a card, in a dialog or on the checklist: the REST API is off ("give it a port on the API &
  monitoring page", and on the REST API's own card, two rows above the port, "give it a port below"), its new port,
  bind address or certificate is saved and not yet applied by the server - where the button opened an address nothing
  listened on until a reinitialise or a restart - it listens on the loopback address and this Control Panel is on
  another machine, or it cannot listen beyond this machine without a certificate. Discovery's sentence for a REST API
  that is off says that the page and the Deck both read the cases over it and to give it a port on the API &
  monitoring page, where it said to turn it on under Settings or read the cases in the Control Deck, whose button
  beside it was disabled for the same reason. The Deck has no address for one of its views, so each button opens the
  Deck itself (the owner's decision of 9 October 2026: deep links where it has them). It is the Control Deck in every
  text: the REST API's card is REST administration API and the Control Deck, where it said Web Control Deck, and the
  sandbox check sends the reader to the Control Deck's delivery queue, where it said the Deck's queue page.

- **Fixed: a dialog's scroll bar was drawn over its fields.** WPF-UI draws a scroll bar over the content it scrolls,
  and a dialog's tabs and its body gave their fields the whole width under it: on the domain dialog's Limits and DKIM
  tabs every text box lost its right border and *Browse…* was cut in half, and the distribution list dialog's hints
  ended under the bar. A tab's fields (`DialogFields.Scroll`) and the frame's body (`DialogFrame`) now keep twelve
  pixels clear of the bar while it shows, and none while the content fits, so that a tab that does not scroll still
  ends its fields where the strip and the Save button end (`Services/ScrollBarInset`). The IP range dialog's General
  tab and the route dialog's Addresses tab no longer scroll by two pixels: the tab control was measured outside its
  window in the system's default font, in which the row of headers is two pixels shorter than the dialog draws it, and
  is now measured in the dialog's own font and rounded up, with four pixels for the layout rounding that the window
  does at 150 % and the measure cannot.

- **Fixed: the tab strips cut their headers mid-word, and the domain and account dialogs showed a third of theirs.**
  An overflowing strip scrolled by pixels - four fifths of its width a chevron click, 48 a wheel notch, Windows' least
  distance for the selected tab - so that it began "… ing and disclaimer" or "… al" and ended "Tagg" or "Ex", and in
  the 640-pixel domain and account dialogs six or seven of seventeen and sixteen headers were in sight. The strip now
  moves by whole headers (`Services/TabStripSnap`): a chevron puts the first header cut or out of sight at the right
  at the left edge, or goes back by as many whole headers as fit, a wheel notch is one header, a tab chosen by
  keyboard or click comes in by a whole-header step, and each chevron is live while a header is cut or hidden on its
  side; an edge that still cuts a header fades over 24 pixels, so that the header reads as one that goes on under the
  chevron. The domain and account dialogs are 800 pixels wide, and the route and IP range dialogs as wide as their
  five headers need in the language in force, where in German "Authentifizierung" and "Schutz" were cut behind the
  chevron (`DialogFields.WidthForTabs`).

- **Fixed: the domain and account dialogs opened at nine tenths of the screen's height whatever the tab held.** They
  gave their tabs the whole height the work area allowed without measuring them - 1,180 pixels on a large screen, the
  domain's General tab three fields above 780 pixels of nothing and Save at the foot of the screen. They are now as
  tall as their tallest tab, no taller than 640 pixels for the tabs and their strip, past which a long form such as
  Limits or DKIM scrolls inside its tab, and no lower than the 360 an embedded list needs (`DialogFields.FitManyTabs`,
  `DialogLayout.ManyTabsCap`).

- **Fixed: most list pages could not be searched, and three searched only on Enter.** The collection lists - the SURBL
  servers, DNS block lists, spam exemptions, blocked senders, the allow and block list, the greylisting exemptions and
  bypass list, blocked attachments, remote domains, server messages and groups - had no search box, so a list of
  hundreds of entries could only be scrolled, and the Groups page had none beside the domains page's two; the public
  folders had none either. Each now has one over its list, named for what it searches, that filters as it is typed in
  over every column the list shows, as the domains, IP ranges and rules pages do. On every list page whose search
  filters the rows it read - these, the routes, TCP/IP ports, IP ranges, SSL certificates, rules, the delivery queue,
  the allowed and blocked domains and the quarantine - the count beside the title says how many the search shows while
  one is typed in ("Shown: 2 of 40"), and where it hides every entry the list says that no entry has what was typed in
  it, where the routes, TCP/IP ports, IP ranges, SSL certificates, rules and delivery queue pages showed an empty list
  and said nothing. The allowed and blocked domains filter as they are typed in where they waited for Enter, and their
  "Entries that match the search" notice no longer stays once the search is cleared; the suppression list and the
  audit trail, whose searches ask the server, search once typing pauses for 300 milliseconds, and at once on Enter.

- **Fixed: the list pages laid out their actions four ways and showed their counts five.** The collection lists put
  Add, Edit, Delete and Refresh in the header, each with a glyph; the routes, TCP/IP ports, IP ranges, SSL
  certificates and rules pages had their verbs in a toolbar, no count and no Refresh, and the message trace F5 alone;
  the delivery queue had its verbs in the header between glyphs and its count in the subtitle; and a count was a pill,
  a caption under the list ("4 public folders."), the subtitle ("4 messages waiting for delivery.", "4 rules of the
  server") or an Information notice ("3 addresses listed.", "5 messages held.", "Entries that match the search: 1 of
  4."). Every list page now has one shape (docs/ControlPanelDesign.md, List pages): the count beside the title as a
  grey pill - "4 routes", "Active: 2 of 3", "Shown: 2 of 40", "1 to 100 of 1284" - that a screen reader hears as it
  changes, as it heard the notices, and Refresh in the header; the search, the filters and the list's verbs in the
  toolbar over the list - the selected entry's Edit or Properties, then Delete, then Add…, the Primary, at the right
  edge - in words without glyphs; and one way to add on each page, the toolbar's Add… or the form under the list. The
