  toolbar puts its actions on a row of their own under the search where the widest of them does not fit beside it, and
  its filters under the search where the two do not fit side by side, so that the suppression list's Remove and Add…,
  which had moved to the header because beside its domain box they were not drawn in the narrowest window, are in its
  toolbar again; the quarantine's Group by is a filter beside its search and Remove expired is in its toolbar, where
  all four were in the header and squeezed its title. Five captions moved their Alt key to leave R to Refresh -
  Deliver lo_cal → remote, Add a ro_ute, Rem_ove criterion, Re_move stored passphrase and Proto_col - and thirty-six
  translated captions moved theirs in their own language.

- **Fixed: the Primary button came first on some pages, in the middle on others and last on the rest.** The REST API
  keys page put Create a key… before Refresh, the event scripts Save & reload before Check syntax and Reload from
  disk, the rules page Add criterion… and Add action… before their Edit and Remove, the SSL certificates page Save
  passphrase before Remove stored passphrase, and Backup & restore's cards changed their order from one to the next,
  Restore the mailbox before Re-read the outcome. One order now holds in every header, toolbar and card footer
  (docs/ControlPanelDesign.md, Rules): the secondary and destructive buttons first, then Refresh or Reload, then the
  Primary - or the act drawn in the filled Danger appearance - at the right edge, as the settings pages' Reload and
  Save changes already were; the delivery queue's Deliver now, the suppression list's Add…, the audit trail's Put back
  and the public folders' Add folder come last with the list page pattern. A dialog keeps the Windows order, its
  primary button before Cancel.

- **Fixed: the editors on the domain, account and route dialogs' tabs drew blue buttons of their own beside the
  dialog's blue Save.** The list editor's Add on the domain's Names and Allow and block list tabs and on the account's
  External tab, the account's Rules tab's Add rule, Add criterion and Add action, App passwords' Create, Two-factor's
  Enrol a second factor, Save levels now on the account's and the domain's Levels tabs, the domain's DKIM tab's Switch
  now and the route's Add address were all Primary buttons, so that a tab could show two blue buttons, each looking
  like the way out of the dialog; and the Rules tab kept the Rules page's 24-pixel padding inside the tab's own, so
  that the rules stood 24 pixels further in than every other tab's content. They are Secondary buttons on those tabs,
  the dialog's Save is its one Primary button, and the Rules tab starts at the dialog's inset as the other tabs do; on
  the Rules page and the list pages Add stays Primary.

- **Fixed: a page's subtitle was squeezed into the column left of its actions, and the long ones pushed the page's
  list below the window.** The greylisting bypass list's subtitle ran to ten lines in English and fourteen in German,
  the allow and block list's to six and eight, Blocked senders' to six, Webmail's to five and TCP/IP ports' to three,
  so that in the narrowest window those pages showed their list's header and no rows. The subtitle has a line of its
  own under the title and the actions, across the header up to 840 pixels (AppSubtitleWidth), and the actions go under
  it only where the title would not fit beside them whole; and those subtitles, and the Administrator roles page's,
  are two sentences at most, the rest being in the help document each page's help opens - and, for the ports page, in
  the Listening column's header, which says that the column is read from this machine's open ports. Every page's
  subtitle is held to two sentences, six still longer listed with why.

- **Fixed: the failure toast was one 1,160-pixel line across the sidebar and the page, with nothing to do but close
  it.** "Server unavailable - Could not load this page: ..." ran from the window's left edge nearly to its right over
  the sidebar's rows and the version footer, centred across the whole window with no width limit, and offered only its
  close button. Toasts now sit over the page, inside the content column, at most 560 pixels wide, so that a long
  sentence wraps to a few lines; and the failure a page reports when it cannot be entered carries Try again, which
  enters the page once more while it is still the page on screen and closes the toast.

- **Fixed: an alias's target was the part of its row the ellipsis took.** The Domains & accounts page drew an alias as
  one trimmed line, "name → target", in a column of about 200 pixels at 1280, so that "info@example.com → user00@ex…"
  lost the delivery address an administrator looks for and a long alias lost the arrow too. Each alias row is now two
  lines, each trimmed with its own tool tip: the alias, and under it in the secondary text "→" and the address it
  delivers to; a screen reader still hears both as one, and the list's floor holds three of the taller rows.

- **Fixed: in a short window the settings pages left their settings a strip 140 pixels high.** On Auto-ban, SSL/TLS,
  Administrative access, Logging, Performance and the other pages built the same way, the title, a two-line subtitle,
  a two-line notice and the tab strip all stayed pinned while only the tab's content scrolled, so that at 760 by 520 a
  tab showed one card heading and two lines of text. The page's notice now sits above the first card of the tab on
  screen and scrolls away with it, moving with the tab chosen, and is scrolled back into view when it has a warning to
  give, as a save that could not write a row does; below 600 pixels of page the subtitle is the title's tool tip (and
  still the header's help text for a screen reader); the header and the tab strip stay pinned.

- **Fixed: the account dialog's External tab left the server, the column that says which mailbox an external account
  collects from, about 110 pixels.** Beside fixed columns for Enabled, the name, the port and the connection security,
  whose cells are the dialog's sentences ("SSL/TLS - encrypted…"), a row read "pop.oldprovide…". The connection
  security is in the account's dialog only, beside the port it goes with, as the server type already was, the name is
  narrower and the port as wide as its five digits, so that the server has some 280 pixels.

- **Fixed: the Levels tab of the domain and account dialogs showed a setting's name without its first underscore.**
  Each setting a level may hold its own value of is a tick box captioned with the server's name for it, and a tick box
  takes the first underscore of its caption as its access key, so that "max_message_size_kb" read "maxmessage_size_kb"
  with Alt+M on it - and every name has an underscore. The names are shown as the server spells them, with no access
  key.

- **Fixed: the Administrator roles grid scrolled sideways at 1280 pixels and cut the sentences it is there to show,
  and the assignments grid filled half its card.** The roles grid's four fixed columns took 910 pixels in a card
  capped at 980 with about 900 for them, so a scroll bar ran under the rows and the purposes and permissions read
  "Reset passwords and unlock accounts in one d..." and "administer_server, administer_domain, view_configuration,
  vi..."; the assignments grid ended some 230 pixels short of its card, and the cards ended short of the header's
  button. The cards are as wide as the page, less the scroll bar's room; Role and Built in are as wide as their words
  in the reader's language and the purpose and the permissions share the rest two to three, the account and its
  domains sharing theirs around the role, each sentence column down to 160 pixels; neither grid scrolls sideways, in
  the narrowest window either; and the purposes and permissions wrap onto as many lines as they need, where they ended
  in an ellipsis.

- **Fixed: the Journaling and dual delivery page's list scrolled sideways, said nothing for a rule that was off, and
  said nothing after an add, a switch or a removal.** Its seven columns were fixed at 1,100 pixels on a card of about
  900, so that the grid scrolled sideways in a 1280 window, the note was never in view, Where it goes was off the card
  in the smallest window, and German cut "Beide Richtungen" to "Beide Richtung" with nothing to say so; the On column
  read Yes or nothing; the button read Switch the rule over whichever way it went; adding, switching and removing a
  rule read the list again without a word; and the add form had no title, wrapped Note onto a line of its own and
  repeated each caption in its box. Whose mail, Where it goes and the note now share the card's width, cut short with
  an ellipsis and whole in a tool tip, and the four short words take their own width, each column floored at its
  header and at the widest word it can show, so that in the smallest window the grid scrolls sideways with every word
  whole; On says On or Off; the button says Turn off or Turn on, by the selected rule; each act reads the list again,
  selects the rule it acted on and says so above the list ("Rule for example.com added.", "Rule for user00@example.com
  turned on."), a refusal at Critical there; and the form, titled Add a journaling rule, lays its boxes out in the
  grid's order, three to a line, with examples in place of the captions - example.com or user@example.com, by the
  choice beside it, and journal@archive.example. `JournalingPageTests` holds the words, the columns, the outcomes and
  the form.

- **Fixed: the Allowed and blocked domains page cut its Added and Note columns with nothing to say so, had no way to
  change an entry, and kept a notice on the page for good.** At 1280 pixels Added read "2026-" and the note "Always
  accept, whatev", four letters wide in German, while the Action column spent about 250 pixels on "Allowed: not
  greylisted, not refused on score" in every row; an entry could only be removed and added again, which gave it
  today's date and a new id; and an Information notice that began with a fragment, "Not the spam exemptions, whose
  senders and IP ranges skip every test...", stood under the toolbar whatever the page showed. Action now says Allowed
  or Blocked, with what each does in the cell's tool tip and in the row's words to a screen reader; Added (server
  time) is the reader's short date and time; every column is trimmed with its whole text in a tool tip and floored at
  its header. Edit…, before Delete, and Enter, F2 or a double-click on a row open the add dialog on the entry, titled
  Edit a domain on the list and headed with its name, whose Save changes it in place over the REST API's `PUT
  /api/v1/domain-policy-list/{id}` - the one interface the server changes an entry through - keeping its id and its
  date, and says a refusal about the pattern under its box and anything else above the fields; the page then keeps the
  entry selected and says it was saved. The dialog opens only once the REST API can be used from here, Edit… and Save
  each asking for the administrator's one-time code again where there is one; where it cannot be used, the page says
  why and opens nothing - the REST API off, as it is by default, with a port to give it on the API & monitoring page,
  or bound to the server's loopback address while this Control Panel runs on another machine, with the Control Deck
  there to use, and either way that the entry can be deleted and added again. The subtitle is two sentences, what the
  list is and which list to use instead, and the notice is gone. `DomainPolicyEditTests` holds the words, the date,
  the request, the columns, the Edit wiring and the dialog's keys against its fields in every catalogue.

- **Fixed: the Discovery page showed nothing while it read the cases, bare headers where it had no lines to show, and
  no row of the lines in the smallest window.** The REST API's reads can take eight seconds, and the page stayed as it
  was meanwhile; the lines' card showed its column headers alone until a case was selected, and where the selected
  case had no lines; its title stood twelve pixels left of every other titled card's, at the list card's eight pixels
  of padding; the Searches, Live holds and Exports counts were left-aligned text; and the two cards, floored at the
  list cards' height and sharing the room, left the lines' grid no row at all in a 760 by 520 window. A ring now says
  "Reading the cases…" in the cases' place from the first request to the last; the lines' card says "Select a case
  above to see its lines on the audit trail." or "The audit trail holds no line for this case." under its headers -
  or, where the audit trail could not be read whole, for want of view_audit or any other refusal the notice above
  says, "This case's lines could not be read; the notice above says why." - and is hidden while there are no cases to
  choose from; it takes the Card's own padding; the counts are right-aligned; and each grid keeps three rows on a
  FillPanel of its own inside a card floored at what it holds, below which the page scrolls, with the case's name and
  a line's detail floored too and cut short with an ellipsis, where the smallest window gave the name nothing ("Co"
  under a header cut to "N..."). `DiscoveryPageTests` holds the counts, the padding, the floors, the empty states and
  the ring.

- **Fixed: the Incoming relays page was a list of strings with no columns, no way to change a relay, and a delete that
  went by the name.** Each row read "Front-end spam filter (203.0.113.40 - 203.0.113.41)", 23 pixels tall, with no
  headers, no search and an outline for a selection; a wrong address meant deleting the relay and adding it again; and
  Delete selected, the page header's only button, recovered the name by splitting the row's text at " (" and deleted
  the first relay of that name, whichever was selected. The page is now a grid of Name, Lower IP and Upper IP, each
  row the relay's own by its id, three rows always in view and the page scrolling below them, under a toolbar with a
  search over the name and both addresses and the row's verbs, Edit… and Delete selected; the count is beside the
  title and Refresh in the header. Edit…, Enter, F2 and a double-click open the relay's dialog, which saves its three
  fields in place, says an empty box under it and the server's refusal above the fields; Delete selected deletes the
  relay by its id and selects the row that took its place among those the search shows. Each says what it did above
  the list ("Front-end spam filter saved.", "... deleted."), a refusal at Critical there where it was a message box.
  `IncomingRelaysPageTests` holds the grid, the id, the delete, the toolbar and the dialog.

- **Fixed: the TCP/IP port dialog was taller than the smallest window, showed rows that did not apply, and never said
  which port it edited.** At 520 by 880 pixels it was taller than a 760 by 520 window, so its body scrolled behind
  Save; SMTP authentication's five-line hint about port 25 stood on POP3 and IMAP ports, where its box was disabled;
  the client-certificate policy's hint and the CA bundle's row stood under a policy of Off; and the title "TCP/IP
  port" and the heading "Port binding" named no port. SMTP authentication is now shown for an SMTP port alone, its
  hint one sentence - the rest is in docs/SmtpAuthOnDeliveryPorts.md - and the CA bundle and what Request and Require
  do are shown while the policy is one of them; the title and the heading name the port as it was read, "SMTP port
  587". `TcpIpPortDialogTests` holds the rows, the hint and the name.

- **Fixed: Directory synchronisation's search filter hid the clause that keeps disabled accounts out, and its cards
  were wider than the form.** The filter was a single line capped at 620 pixels, with about 200 pixels of its card
  unused, and its placeholder - the only place the product stated the default filter - was cut at
  "...(!(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.80", the start of the clause the caption is about; a placeholder cannot
  be scrolled and is gone once the box has text. The cards were 860 pixels wide against the form width of 760 the
  Directory authentication (LDAP) page and the settings pages keep. The filter box is now the width of its card, wraps
  over two lines at least - its placeholder with it - and is in the monospaced face, and its hint names the default in
  the sentence that says what it takes, "The default,
  (&(objectClass=user)(objectCategory=person)(mail=*)(!(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=2))), takes enabled
  person objects that carry a mail address", in view whatever the box holds; Directory authentication's user search
  filter is shown the same way, its hint naming the shipped filter where it said "the shipped filter shown in grey";
  and the cards are at the form width. `LdapFilterFieldTests` holds the boxes, the cards and each default to the
  server's own constant in LdapSettings.cpp, character for character.

- **Fixed: the Setup checklist named its next step without leading to it, below every finished item at full size.** On
  a server that had done the first four items the summary said "Next step: Passwords only over TLS…" with nothing to
  press, and the step was off-screen under four Done cards, each with its description, its finding and its Open
  button, which a returning administrator scrolled past on every visit. The summary now carries Go to the next step,
  which brings the marked card on screen and puts the keyboard on its Open button; and an item that is Done or Not
  needed is one line - its number, its pill, its title and its Open button - with a chevron beside Open, and a click
  on it or on the title, that shows what the item is for and what was found, and stays open while the page draws the
  list again after its DNS lookups. Action needed and Cannot tell keep their whole text. `SetupChecklistNextStepTests`
  holds the button, where it goes and the one-line items.

- **Fixed: the Welcome page's sample-domain offer assumed an empty server, and two stacked notices pushed the task
  list down.** "Nothing on this server to look at yet? This makes example.test…" showed whenever example.test was
  absent, on a server of four domains and eleven accounts as on a new one; it was a second purple Information notice
  under the walk's, four lines at 1280 pixels and seven at 760, and repeated the password sentence its dialog shows;
  it arrived after the first paint and moved the intents about 80 pixels under the pointer; and at 760 pixels no
  intent was on screen. The walk's offer is now the one notice above the intents, and the sample is a card under them
  titled A sample domain - "Makes example.test with three mailboxes, a distribution list, a rule and some delivered
  mail, so that every page has something in it. Remove it before this server takes real mail." - with Make a sample
  domain, or Remove the sample domain, in its footer. The card is drawn as the page is and its button pressed once the
  read lands; what the read found is a notice in the card at its level, Good for the sample that is here (with how to
  be given another password, which the creation dialog alone shows), Warning for a domain of that name that is not
  the sample - with Open Domains - and for a domain table the server could not read. `WelcomeSampleCardTests` holds
  the card, its place and its states.

- **Fixed: the Setting profiles page named the applied profile by its key, and its six controls wrapped with two
  confusable Keep buttons.** "The small-office profile is applied." said the key, in German and Japanese as well,
  where the list, the setup checklist and the other confirmations said "Small office", and the Apply and Put back
  questions and the lines that say what they did used the key too; the 430-pixel list of profiles and five buttons
  wrapped onto two rows at 1280 pixels and three at 760, with "Keep its settings, forget the way back" beside "Keep
  the shipped settings", which mean different things; Refresh was in that row where the sibling pages have it in the
  header; the list's items were sentences ("Small office - settings that would change on this server: 3 of 31."); and
  the table's last column, "Asks for a confirmation", held notes that are not confirmations. The profile is named by
  its title everywhere; Refresh is in the header; Put back what it changed and Discard the previous settings, as the
  way back's two acts, and Keep the shipped settings, while no profile is in effect, are the applied notice's own,
  each shown while it can be taken, so that the two never show together and the row beside the list holds the list and
  Apply this profile, and the notice of a profile that could not be applied in full names the acts it shows - "Put
  back what it changed, or discard the previous settings to keep what it wrote, then apply it again." with a way back,
  and "Apply it again, or keep the shipped settings." with none, where it said "Put back what it wrote, or keep it" of
  an act the page no longer has; each profile in the list is its title with "Would change here: 3 of 31" beside it in
  the caption colour; and the column is Notes. `ProfilesPageFlowTests` holds the titles, the acts and the list.

- **Fixed: the Dashboard's attention card filled the first screen, the Server status page's configuration warnings
  never reached it, and its figures led nowhere.** The card listed every open step of the setup checklist - eleven to
  fourteen rows, 330 to 400 pixels on a new server - so that the figures began 577 to 650 pixels down and both charts
  were below the fold at 1280 by 800, for a list that is the Setup checklist one click away; an open relay, a missing
  host name, refused bounces and localhost banned were said on Server status alone; and the five figures were cards
  that could not be pressed. The card now lists the configuration warnings first, the most severe first, each with its
  mark and a button to the page that puts it right, and is Critical while an IP range relays for anybody; then the
  checklist's next step and two more; then "8 more steps on the Setup checklist", which opens it. No host name, which
  is a warning and the checklist's host-name step at once, is the step alone while the step is open, so that the card
  lists and counts it once. The checks are read by one piece of code for both pages (Services/ConfigurationChecks), so
  that they cannot disagree. Each figure is a button to the page it is read on - Uptime and Messages processed to
  Server status, In queue to the Delivery queue, Spam detected to the spam overview and Viruses removed to the virus
  overview - drawn as the card was, with the hover of a card that can be pointed at and a focus ring that moves
  nothing, and named as its figure is, the label first. `DashboardAttentionTests` holds the arithmetic, the order, the
  card's level, the host name counted once and the buttons, and `StatusWarningLevelTests` holds each check's level and
  page where the checks now are.

- **Fixed: nothing signed out of the Control Panel, connected it to another server or led back from Connection lost
  short of closing the program.** The administrator's menu held who was signed in, the version, the language, the
  theme and About; the sign-in page came back only after a cancelled second factor, which left the session the current
  one, signed in on its password; and with the link lost the pill read "Connection lost", its tool tip and accessible
  name repeating the two words, with nothing that said the Control Panel tries again or offered to sign in again. The
  menu now ends with Connect to another server… and Sign out, and starts with Sign in again while the link is lost.
  Each asks about the page's unsaved changes first, as every way off a page does, then ends any tour, leaves the page
  and lets go of every page built for the session, clears the history, puts the navigation, the search and the help
  away, hides the breadcrumb and the pending bar, ends the session - the server's object released and the password
  forgotten (ServerSession.SignOut) - and shows the sign-in page on the server and the account that were signed in,
  the keyboard in the password, or in the server's box with its name chosen to type another; a refused second factor
  goes the same way. The pill's tool tip and name say what happens next: "Reconnecting to mail.example.com - what is
  on screen may be out of date" and "Connection to mail.example.com lost - the Control Panel tries again on your next
  action; nothing can be saved until it is back". `SignOutTests` holds the menu, the steps and the session's end, and
  `ConnectionStatusTests` the sentences.

- **Fixed: Pause meant two things on neighbouring pages, and a paused server was invisible everywhere else.** Server
  status's Pause stops the mail server's engine - no connection is accepted and nothing is delivered - and Live logs'
  Pause, with the same glyph, only freezes the view; once the engine was paused, the status pill still said Connected
  in green on every page, since only the link fed it and nothing outside Server status read the server's state, so a
  pause that was forgotten was a server that took no mail with no sign of it. Server status's buttons are now Pause
  the mail server and Resume the mail server, and its State reads Paused, where it read Stopped; Live logs' are Pause
  view and Resume view, with a glyph of their own. While the server reports Stopped, the window shows a Warning bar at
  its foot under every page, "The mail server is paused - nothing is accepted or delivered.", with Resume the mail
  server, the words of Server status's own button without its Alt key, and the pill says Paused at the Warning level,
  "Connected to mail.example.com as Administrator - the mail server is paused" in its tool tip; the state is asked as
  each page is entered and on the Dashboard's two-second refresh, and Server status hands it the state it reads, so
  that its Pause and Resume show at once. F6 reaches the bar with the pending bar. `ServerPausedTests` holds the
  words, the bar, the pill and where the state is asked.

- **Fixed: the sign-in card's two-factor link set up the weaker option, and the two code prompts looked the same.**
  "Set up two-factor authentication…" on the sign-in card opened the Control-Panel-only setup, which Administrative
  access calls an older, weaker option; the server's code prompt and this computer's were the same dialog, titled
  "Two-factor authentication", so that with both on the administrator was asked twice by identical dialogs for codes
  from two entries of the authenticator; and the setup dialog had the same title and paired Enable two-factor
  authentication with Close. The link is gone - both factors are set up on Administrative access's Two-factor tab,
  after sign-in; the prompts are headed "The server's administrator code" and "This computer's Control Panel code",
  each with a sentence that says which entry of the authenticator it wants; and the setup dialog is titled by its act,
  "Set up Control-Panel-only two-factor authentication" or "Turn off Control-Panel-only two-factor authentication", as
  the tab's button that opens it is, with Cancel beside its act until it is done and Close after.
  `TwoFactorPromptsTests` holds the card, the prompts and the dialog.

- **Fixed: the Groups page's Members… was a lone button under the list, and a double-click on a group renamed it.**
  Add, Edit and Delete were in the toolbar over the list and Refresh in the header, but Members… - what a group is
  for - sat under the list, 760 pixels down at 1280 by 800, beside a hint that changed as a group was chosen and was
  never announced; Enter and a double-click on a group opened the rename. Members… is now the list's first verb,
  before Edit, Delete and Add, enabled while a group is selected; Enter and a double-click on a group open its
  members, and F2 is Edit, the rename. What the hint said is the subtitle's and the empty state's, and the list
  editor takes such a verb of a row from any page built on it (`CollectionEditorView.AddRowVerb`,
  `GridKeys.WireRename`). Members… has an Alt key of its own beside Edit, Delete, Add and Refresh in every language,
  where the French and Italian Members… had Edit's and the Russian Delete's, so that the key moved between the two
  rather than opening either. `GroupsPageVerbsTests` holds the verb, its place, the keys and the five Alt keys.

- **Fixed: a group's Add account… was a drop-down of every account on the server, the members among them, that could
  not be typed in.** With hundreds of mailboxes there was no way to find one but to scroll, an account picked that was
  a member already was refused only after the pick, and accounts went in one at a time. Add account… now opens a list
  under a search box of the accounts that are not members yet, filtered as the search is typed in; several can be
  chosen with Ctrl and Shift, and Enter - in the search box, the one account the search leaves - or Add puts them in
  the group, which says what it added ("dave@example.com added to the group.", "3 accounts added to the group.") and
  selects the first of them in the member list. An account another session made a member meanwhile is not given a
  second row; with every account a member already, the dialog says so in place of the list. `GroupMemberCandidatesTests`
  holds the list, the words and the picker.

- **Fixed: the Public folders page told the reader to "use the hierarchy delimiter" to make sub-folders, which made
  folders a mail client cannot open, and listed the folders flat.** The page never named the delimiter or showed the
  hierarchy - Sales and Sales.Leads were two rows side by side - and the server's Add took "Sales.Leads" as one folder's
  name at the top, while the server finds a folder by splitting its path at the delimiter and walking down from the top,
  so that such a folder could be listed but not opened. The page now reads the folders' tree through each folder's
  sub-folders and lists each under its parent, a level further in, with a folder's glyph, and the subtitle names the
  server's delimiter in an example ("Sales.Leads puts Leads under Sales"). Add folder asks for the name in a dialog that
  says what the delimiter does, opens on the selected folder's name and the delimiter, has Create in place of OK,
  pressed only once a name is typed, and makes each folder of the name under the one before it, as a mail client's
  CREATE does; a name with an empty part, too long or too deep, or of a folder that is there already, is said under the
  box, and the new folder is selected. Delete's question says how many sub-folders go with the folder ("Delete the
  public folder Sales, its 2 sub-folders and every message in them?"), and a folder whose own name holds the delimiter
  is pointed out above the list; such a folder does not stop Add folder making the sub-folder its name spells, as the
  warning says it does, since a folder is told from another by its path and not by its names joined - the misnamed
  Projects.2025 at the top and Projects' 2025 are two. A sub-folder's Permissions open on the sub-folder, which the
  permissions dialog looked for at the top alone. The help page both pages open (PublicFoldersAndGroups.md) says how the
  tree, the delimiter, the refusals, a misnamed folder and Delete's sub-folders work, and on the Groups side Members…
  with Enter, the double-click and F2, and the account picker. `PublicFolderTreeTests` holds the tree, the checks, the
  words and the page's reads and writes.

- **Fixed: a TLS port added on the TCP/IP ports page had no certificate and did not start, and every change to a port
  asked to reinitialise the server there and then.** The add form offered SSL/TLS and both STARTTLS modes but no
  certificate, so the port it added had none and came up "Not listening"; the port's dialog saved such a port with
  "(none)" too; and a Yes/No question to reinitialise followed every add, edit, delete and restore. The add form now has
  a Certificate box, enabled while the security is not None, and refuses a TLS port without one under the box ("Choose
  the certificate this port presents.", or, where the server has none yet, that one is to be added on the SSL
  certificates page first); the dialog's Save refuses it the same way. A change is said by a notice above the list -
  "Ports changed - the server goes on listening on the old set until it is reinitialised." - with Reinitialise now,
  from the first change in a session until the server is reinitialised from the page or the pending bar's Apply now,
  or the service restarted; Restore defaults, which replaces every port, still asks. The form is on two lines where
  one line would leave its boxes too narrow. `PortChangesTests` holds the rules, the words and the page's wiring.

- **Fixed: a rule added on the Rules page was not selected and started switched on, Add criterion… and Add action…
  answered a press with no rule in a message box, and the IF and THEN cards were blank.** The reload after Add rule
  cleared the selection, so the new rule - the list's last row, often out of view - had to be found and clicked; the two
  Add buttons were live with no rule selected and said "Select a rule first."; with no rule, and with a rule that had no
  criteria or actions, both cards were empty and said nothing; a new rule was live before it had its criteria and
  actions; "Enable / disable" never said which it would do; and a switched-off rule differed only by "No" in its last
  column. A new rule is now selected and in view with the keyboard on Add criterion…, starts switched off, and a notice
  under the add form says so with Enable now in it, the toolbar's Enable being scrolled out of view by then ("Spam to
  junk added, switched off: Enable now switches it on once it has a criterion and an action."), the button pressed only
  once the rule has a criterion and an action, when the notice says so and the keyboard goes to it, and then "Spam to
  junk switched on."; the two Add buttons and the match list wait for a rule; each card says what its emptiness means -
  choose a rule above, or that a rule with no criteria matches no message (the server runs a rule's actions only once a
  criterion is met) and one with no actions does nothing; the switch reads Enable or Disable for the selected rule; and
  a switched-off rule's row is in the secondary text colour. `RuleCardsTests` holds the words, the add, the gate, the
  switch, the cards and the row's colour.

- **Fixed: the IP ranges page showed relaying apart from its authentication, said nothing of an open relay, and called
  every permission by another name than the range's dialog.** The permissions card had "Deliver remote → remote (relay)"
  while "Require auth: external to external" was on a tab of the dialog alone, so that unticking relay on the shipped
  Internet range stopped roaming users sending mail and ticking it on a range that asked for no authentication made an
  open relay, with no word either way; and the card said "Allow SMTP", "Require TLS for auth" and "remote" where the
  dialog said "Allow SMTP connections", "Require SSL/TLS when authenticating" and "external" - four names for the TLS
  box in all. The card and the dialog now say the same: Allow SMTP connections, Allow IMAP connections, Allow POP3
  connections, Require TLS before authentication, and each delivery direction - Local to local, Local to external,
  External to local, External to external (relay) - on a row of its own under Allow delivery, with Only after SMTP
  authentication beside it, which follows it; the dialog's Relaying and Require auth tabs are one Delivery tab of the
  same rows. A range wider than one address that lets External to external through without authentication, or Local to
  external - which relays for whoever gives one of this server's domains as the sender, since the server takes the
  sender from MAIL FROM - is said under the rows with the direction to tick Only after SMTP authentication for, at
  Critical, "an open relay", where it reaches the Internet and as a warning inside a private network, and its
  permissions are asked about before they are saved, on the page and in the dialog, whose tabs are as tall as the
  Delivery tab with the longest of its notices, which a shorter tab cut off. The setup checklist, the steps of the
  office, gateway and relay setting profiles (shown on the Setting profiles page) and the help page the TCP/IP ports
  page opens (SecureDefaults.md) name the box by its new caption. Server status's configuration check, which the
  Dashboard's attention card shares, counts an open relay the same way: either direction without authentication on a
  range that reaches the Internet is Critical, Local to external alone as "IP range 'Office' allows local-to-external
  delivery without authentication, so anyone in it who gives one of this server's domains as the sender can relay mail
  through this server (open relay risk).", where only External to external was, on any range; a single address and a
  private network's range, whose External to external it marked Critical as well, are the page's to mark.
  `RelayExposureTests` holds the reach of a range, the words, the card, the dialog and the question.

- **Fixed: a range added on the IP ranges page was not selected and said nothing of what it could do, and the list was
  not in priority order.** A new range may connect but delivers in no direction, so it can send no mail until its
  permissions are chosen; yet the reload after Add left the selection where it was, and the permissions card went on
  showing another range - the palette's "Let a device send mail" led here and then said no more - and the rows were in
  the order the server listed them, though where ranges overlap the higher priority wins. The new range is now
  selected, its card brought to the top of the page with the keyboard in it, and the card says what to do next
  ("Office printers added. Addresses in the range may connect, but send no mail until you choose what they may deliver
  and Save permissions.") until its permissions are saved, on the card or in Properties…, or another range is shown; a
  search that would hide the new range is cleared. The list is ordered by priority, the highest first and the ranges
  of one priority by name; a header clicked orders it by its column - Priority's turns the order round - and that
  order is kept when the list is read again. `IPRangeAddedTests` holds the add, the notice and the order.

- **Fixed: the Auto-ban page listed no ban, and lifting one took four steps across two pages.** "Clear logon-failure
  list" said outright that it lifted no ban; the IP ranges page drew the server's bans - the expiring ranges named
  "Auto-ban: ..." - among the permanent ranges with no column to tell them apart and no filter, so lifting one meant
  opening IP ranges, searching, picking the row by its address and deleting it. The Auto-ban page now opens on Banned
  now: each ban's address, why it was banned - the user name a run of failed sign-ins was guessing at, the spam trap,
  the null sender or the sign-in attempt on a delivery port, without the counter the server adds to the name of a second
  ban for the same user name or trap, "(1)" - and when it ends, "23 min from now" from a Control Panel on the server
  itself and the server's time from one elsewhere, with Lift ban on its row (a 24-pixel button named for the row) and
  under the list (Delete on the row presses it); Lift ban asks first, Cancel taking Enter, deletes the range by its id
  as IP ranges does, and says "The ban on 198.51.100.77 is lifted." The IP ranges page has an Expires column - Never, or
  when an expiring range ends - a Relay column that counts a relay in either direction to an external address, as the
  range's permissions card does, and says No, After sign-in, Without sign-in for one address such as My computer and, as
  a Warning pill, for a private network's range, or Open relay as a Critical pill for a range that reaches the Internet,
  and Show auto-bans only, which narrows the list to the bans and counts them as a search does ("Shown: 1 of 5"). Server
  status's ban count opens Banned now. `BannedNowTests` holds the words, the order of the page, the question, the
  columns and the filter; docs/AutoBan.md says where the bans are and what Lift ban does.

- **Fixed: the SSL certificates page could not change a certificate, never said which ports use one, and sorted its
  Certificate column by the status word.** A certificate whose file had moved - "File missing" - could be put right
  only by deleting it and adding it again, which gave it a new id and left every TCP/IP port that presented the old
  one with no certificate, so that it did not start; no column said which ports present each, though the page's
  purpose is "which port uses which"; the search found the page for "PFX" while the form took PEM alone and said
  nothing of a .pfx; and the Certificate column put "Expired" beside the good ones by its word. Edit… in the toolbar,
  Enter, F2 and a double-click open the certificate's name and its two files in a dialog that saves them in place,
  its id kept, says an empty box under it and the server's refusal above the fields, and the page then says
  "mail.example.com saved. The TCP/IP ports that present it read its files again when the server is next
  reinitialised."; a Used by column names the ports ("SMTP 465, IMAP 993", Not used, or Not known when the ports could
  not be read), and the details card of the selected certificate names them whole, which the column cuts for a
  certificate on three ports at 1280 by 800; the form and the dialog say that the server reads PEM and give the two
  openssl commands that make a .pfx or .p12 into it; the Certificate column sorts by how much a certificate asks for
  attention and then by how soon it expires; and Delete selected says what it deleted and selects the row that took
  its place, after the question that already named the ports. `CertificatesEditTests` holds the order, the column,
  the details card's ports, the dialog's save by id and the wiring.

- **Fixed: the SSL certificates page's add and passphrase flows said nothing, and their controls stayed live whatever
  the state.** A certificate added was neither selected nor said, and its name had to be typed although the subject
  is in the file; the form's five fields shared one line, so that the passphrase's caption wrapped to two lines in
  English and three in German and the path boxes were 100 pixels wide at 760; Remove stored passphrase could be
  pressed with nothing stored and Save passphrase with an empty box, which answered with a message box; the passphrase
  editor was offered for a key that needs none; and the Name column was cut at 170 pixels while the paths, the same
  folder on every row, took the rest. The form is now two lines of two fields - the name and the passphrase, then the
  two files - with Add in its card's footer; choosing the certificate file fills in the name from the certificate's
  subject while the box is empty; an added certificate is selected and scrolled to, and the page says
  "mail.example.com added. Choose it for a port on the TCP/IP ports page to use it." with Open TCP/IP ports; Remove
  stored passphrase can be pressed while one is stored or the page cannot tell, and Save passphrase while its box
  holds one; for a key the page read as unencrypted with none stored, the editor waits behind Set a passphrase
  anyway…; a saved or removed passphrase, and a refusal, is said on the page where it was a message box; each
  outcome is said in a notice above the list that is scrolled into view, since at 1280 by 800 the page scrolls to
  reach Add and the passphrase; and every column of the grid is a share of its width over a floor, the Name column's
  the largest, so that a name is whole at 1280 by 800, while the path columns show the file's name, the whole path
  in the tool tip, and the headers wrap at their spaces, so that each is whole in every language - "Private
  Schlüsseldatei" was cut to "Private Schlüss…" in German. `CertificatesAddFlowTests` holds the form, the name, the
  outcome and where it is said, the buttons, the columns and their headers.

- **Fixed: the Automatic certificates (ACME) page put its issued certificate below the fold, and blamed the network
  for a host-name list that was empty.** The card's one live fact - a certificate issued and valid until a date, near
  its end, expired, or none yet - was its last row, under seven fields and below the fold at 1280 by 800; with Issue
  and renew automatically ticked and no host name, the page saved it and then said that no certificate had been
  issued yet and that, if that persisted, the CA could not reach this server, while the server - which splits the
  list at commas as the page now does - asks the CA for nothing without a name; and the ACME directory URL had no
  placeholder. The certificate's state is now the card's first row, with Open SSL certificates beside an issued
  certificate; with the switch on and no host name the row says at Critical, and alone, "No certificate can be
  issued without a host name: add at least one to the host names below.", and goes as a name is typed; and the
  directory shows the Let's Encrypt URL. `AcmeCertificateStateTests` holds the list's reading, the row's place, its
  order and its action.

- **Fixed: the Browse Active Directory dialog said every state as one grey line, left Search live when nothing could
  be searched, and had a search box with no caption.** Active Directory not reachable from this computer, no domain,
  a list or a search that failed, a search under way and what it found were each one line of caption text under the
  list, with no mark and no next step, the reason Windows gave joined on after a dash; where nothing could be
  searched the domain list and the box were greyed and Search was not, and pressing it said "Select a domain
  first."; Domain was a 12-pixel caption beside its list; and the search box had no caption or placeholder, only an
  accessible name. The status is now a notice at the level of what it says - Warning where Active Directory cannot
  be reached or has no domain, "Active Directory cannot be reached from this computer, so its accounts cannot be
  browsed here. Windows reported: ...", Critical for a list or a search that failed, Information while searching and
  for what a search found; Search is disabled with the domain list and the box; and the domain and the name are
  captioned fields on one line, Active Directory domain and Name or account, the name's box saying "Part of a name
  (empty lists everyone)". `ActiveDirectoryPickerStatusTests` holds the levels, Search, the fields and the reason.

- **Fixed: Server status said a paused server as a plain word, and the update steps were three equal buttons that held
  up the window.** State was body text - "Stopped" for a server paused from that very page - and a paused engine raised
  no notice; Check for updates, Download update and Install update were three equal buttons, the two that did not apply
  greyed with no reason given, since a disabled button shows no tool tip, and Install wrapped to a line of its own;
  Check and Download ran on the UI thread behind a wait cursor, Download's tool tip saying that the Control Panel waits
  while it does; and the update-install window drew its steps as hollow circles in the text colour, whether done or
  failed. Server status's State is now a pill at its level - Running Good, Paused and Draining Warning, Starting and
  Stopping Information - and a paused engine is said, with Resume, by the bar at the window's foot that says it on every
  page (the entry on Pause above). The Updates page offers one step at a time as its Primary - Check for updates until a
  release is known, then Download update, then Install update, with Check again before it - and none while an install is
  under way; each step runs off the UI thread with a line in the card that says which, "Downloading 6.3.7…", and holds
  every step until it is done, a Reload meanwhile included, while the rest of the page can be used. The install window's
  steps are the status marks in their levels' colours: finished Good, failed Critical, skipped Warning, under way
  Information. `ServerStatusFlowTests` holds the state's words and levels, the step for every update state, one paused
  notice, the one step, its thread and its hold, and the marks.

- **Fixed: the delivery queue acted on one message of the several chosen, did not say why a message waits, and led
  nowhere from a message to its trace.** Several rows could be chosen, but Deliver now and Remove acted on the first
  alone - Remove asked about one message and removed one; the page's subtitle promised why each message is waiting and
  no column said it - the server's flag for a message being delivered now was read and dropped; nothing led from a
  queued message to the Message trace page that follows it; and the ID was a wide right-aligned number while From and
  Recipients shrank to a word in a narrow window. Deliver now and Remove now act on every row chosen - Remove after one
  question that names the one message, or counts them and says that none of them bounces - and their outcomes count
  them, "3 messages will be tried again now.", in the words a retry of one message has (the entry on the monitoring
  pages' words below); a message the server refuses to remove is named with its reason after those removed before it.
  Deliver all now delivers the whole queue. A State column, in the place of Next try, says where each message stands -
  Delivering now, Due for delivery, Next try in 12 min with the time in its tool tip, or, connected to another computer,
  whose clock may not be this one's, the next try in the reader's date and time marked "(server time)" - and sorts the
  messages being delivered first and then by their next try. Trace message, in the toolbar and as each row's own icon,
  opens the Message trace page with every event of that message, oldest first, as its Follow this message does - or, for
  a message whose id is past the 2147483647 the trace keeps, says so there and to search for its sender or a recipient
  instead. The ID column is narrow and left-aligned, and From, Recipients and State keep a width the grid scrolls
  sideways for. `DeliveryQueueTests` holds the state words and their order, the outcomes, the question and the page's
  lines.

- **Fixed: the Auto-ban page kept its two never-ban lists in two shapes, and an address entry the server ignored was
  said only in its error log.** The list by address, `AutoBanNeverBan`, was one comma-separated box saved with Save
  beside the list by reverse name, a table whose buttons write at once; what a block such as 203.0.113.5/24 spared
  was left to the reader's arithmetic, and an entry the server could not read - "192.168.1", a host name - protected
  nothing without a word on the page. Never auto-ban these addresses is now a table like the names list: each address
  or block with what it covers - One address, "203.0.113.0 - 203.0.113.255", or "Ignored: not an address or a block",
  with a warning that names every entry the server ignores - and Add address... and Remove address, which read the
  list again and write it at once. The Add dialog takes an address or a CIDR block as the server reads one - four
  decimal parts with no leading zero, a prefix no longer than the address - and says under its box an entry it would
  not read or one listed already; Remove asks first. Every button of the Auto-ban tab - Banned now's, the two
  tables' and the page's Reload and Save changes - has an Alt key of its own in English and in each of the
  seventeen languages, Add address... Alt+D beside Add name...'s Alt+A, which `build/check-mnemonics.py` now holds
  on every tab where a settings page places a row of its own. `NeverBanAddressListTests` holds the server's reading
  of an entry, what each row covers, the refusals and the page's row, and `AccessKeysTests` the tab's keys.

- **Fixed: Live logs had no way to narrow a busy log to the message being followed, no legend for its colours, and the
  sideways scroll bar covered the newest line.** The page offered Pause and Clear view over a screenful of lines a
  second (review finding F250). It now has a filter over the lines - every word typed in must be in a line, an
  address, a host or any word of the text, and session=42 names a session exactly, where 42 alone is in the times and
  thread numbers of every other line - and a box for each line type, SMTP, IMAP, POP3, Application, Debug and Errors,
  each drawn in its lines' colour so that the boxes are the colours' legend; a line of a type no box names (a TCP/IP
  line, a script's event) is always shown. The SMTP and POP3 clients' lines take their protocol's colour, where they
  were the default colour beside the servers' green and amber. Wrap lines folds a long line at the log's width instead
  of scrolling sideways; the count beside the title says how many lines are held, or "Shown: 8 of 461" while the
  filter or a box hides some, and a filter that hides every line says so in the log's place; the log keeps its newest
  line clear of the sideways scroll bar, which WPF-UI draws over it; and the toolbar and the log scroll under the
  header in the narrowest window, the log floored at three lines' height, where its empty state's sentence was cut to
  its glyph, and the page stays where it is while the log follows its newest line, so that the filter box stays in
  view as lines stream in. `LiveLogFilesTests` holds the line types, the filter and the page's wiring.

- **Fixed: the Message trace page never said whether tracing was on, following a message threw the search's results
  away, and its Status column was a bare reply code.** The same Information notice - that the trace records nothing
  until message tracing is switched on - stood above a blank grid whatever the setting; "Follow this message" replaced
  the address's results with no way back, and Enter and a double-click did nothing; and Status read 250, 451 or 550,
  right-aligned like a count (review finding F253). The page now reads MessageTraceEnabled and the retention as it
  opens: while tracing is off a Warning says "Message tracing is off - nothing is being recorded." with Open Logging,
  and while it is on a caption says how long events are kept ("Events are kept 30 days."). Before the first search the
  list's place says to enter an address and press Search. A message followed from the results offers Back to results
  for the address, which puts the results back as they were with the event it was followed from selected; Enter, F2
  and a double-click on an event follow its message, as its button does. A status is a pill of its word and level -
  "OK 250", "Deferred 451", "Refused 550" - sorted by the code, and Ctrl+C on an event copies its status in those
  words. `MessageTraceStatusTests` holds the words and the page's wiring.

- **Fixed: the audit trail offered Put back on rows it could not put back, its pager never disabled, its columns
  showed the server's tokens, and its search matched the administrator alone.** Put back was the page's Primary and
  pressable on every row, answering a notice on a domain's or an account's; Newer stayed pressable on the first page
  and Older on the last, and at 760 they wrapped onto different rows; Interface, Object and Action read control_panel,
  role_assignment and password_reset in every language; the Detail column got some 60 pixels ("60 -> 1..."); and the
  search asked the server for the administrator's name (review finding F254). Put back is now a secondary button
  pressable only on a setting's change that records its values - not on a secret's, whose row says "(changed)" - with
  a tool tip that says why on any other row, and its question names both values: "Put AutoBanMinutes back from "120"
  to "60"?". Newer and Older are under the list with the page between them, each pressable only where there is a page
  that way, and one pressed from the keyboard onto the first or the last page hands the keyboard to the other. The
  interfaces, the objects and the actions are the reader's words - "Control Panel or script" for COM, "REST API",
  "Control Deck", "Role assignment", "Password reset" - for every object type and action the server records, among
  them "DNS block list", "Spam exemptions entry", "Allowed or blocked domain", "Never-ban name" and "Directory opt-out
  changed", in every language, and a word a newer server writes is shown readable. The time keeps the width of its
  widest digits, each column of words is floored at the widest of its words on the page, up to 180 pixels, and Detail
  takes twice a share and never less than 200 pixels, its arrow drawn as one ("60 → 120"); where they do not fit the
  grid scrolls sideways, rather than cut who made a change and what it was made to. The search looks in who, what, how
  and the detail of every change: the trail is read whole off the window's thread the first time, a thousand rows a
  call, and each word typed in after is looked for in it. `AuditTrailPageTests` holds the words, the search and the
  page's wiring.

- **Fixed: the quarantine's allow and block icons differed only by colour, its header's four icons acted with nothing
  checked, and a group's row showed neither the pointer nor the keyboard inside it.** Each row, group and the header
  carried a check, a cross and the same list glyph twice, told apart by colour and fill alone - 28 coloured glyphs on
  screen; the header's were full colour and pressable with nothing checked and on an empty page, answering "Check the
  messages first"; and a group's row had no hover or focus-within state, its box and icons 8 to 10 pixels left of the
  rows' (review finding F260). Allow and block are now a person each - PersonAvailable and PersonProhibited - outlined
  as the other two are. The header's four icons are gone: a bar under the toolbar says how many messages are checked
  ("2 messages checked", a polite live region) and carries Release, Allow sender..., Block sender... and Delete
  permanently in words, each pressable only while a message is checked - one pressed from the keyboard leaves the
  keyboard on the list once its act has cleared the checks - and the column of each row's icons is headed Actions. A
  group's row takes the grid's hover grey under the pointer, keeping its selection fill when selected, and its focus
  ring while the keyboard is on its box or one of its icons, and its box and icons line up with the rows'. Release's
  question answers with Re_lease, Alt+L, as the bar's Release does, where Refresh has R on the page.
  `QuarantinePageTests` holds the shapes, the bar and the group's states.

- **Fixed: the quarantine's allow chose the list that does not stop the next hold, and the list dialog's failures were
  plain text.** Allow sender preselected the sender's address on the server's allow and block list whatever had held
  the messages, though its own note said that a message the server-wide spam score holds during the SMTP conversation
  is still held - which is how most quarantined messages got there; and the plan, a preview that could not be made,
  the messages that cannot be listed and the public-suffix warning were one block of plain text, the Primary disabled
  with no reason (review finding F262). The page now tells the dialog whether the server-wide score held any of the
  messages - a score at or over the server's refuse threshold, which only the hold during the SMTP conversation
  records, never a rule's, the sandbox's or an account's own threshold, and never a block-list or impersonation hold,
  which record 0 - and an allow of such messages preselects the domain on the list of allowed and blocked domains, the
  list that stops it, while every other hold keeps the address, which stops a block-list hold and an account's
  threshold where the domain does not; with the address chosen, a Warning under it says "This will not stop the next
  message from this sender being held if it scores 20 or more.", with the server's threshold. A preview that could not
  be made is a Critical notice with Try again, the messages that cannot be listed a Warning, and a public suffix a
  Warning holding the List it anyway box; a request that would write nothing says so. `QuarantineListDialogTests`
  holds which holds the score made and the dialog's wiring.

- **Fixed: Anti-spam settings called the refuse threshold the delete threshold, saved thresholds that contradict each
  other, and said how many settings a save wrote rather than what it changed.** The threshold that refuses a message
  during the SMTP conversation, or holds it in the quarantine, was labelled "Spam delete threshold (score)"; a refuse
  threshold at or below the mark threshold - tested first, so no message is ever marked and delivered - or both at 0
  saved with "Saved 51 settings - applied immediately"; the Quarantine card, which changes what that threshold does,
  was fourth on General and below the fold; the rspamd hook sat on a tab called SpamAssassin; and the Spam traps tab
  said the traps are declared in the Control Deck without saying whether any domain had one (review finding F263). The
  field is now "Spam refuse threshold (score)", its hint saying older versions called it the delete threshold, and
  every text that named the delete threshold - the Quarantine card, the quarantine's empty states, the pipeline's
  note, the SPF softfail hint - says refuse threshold. As the two are typed, a refuse threshold at or below a mark
  threshold above 0 is marked on its field ("The refuse threshold must be above the mark threshold, 5: …") and a save
  writes nothing and says so, and a threshold at 0 is a Warning under the two saying what 0 means. The Quarantine card
  is second on General; the SpamAssassin tab is Content filters, holding SpamAssassin and the external filtering hook,
  the search finds it by rspamd, Content filters and both names of the threshold, and the documentation names the tab
  so; the Spam traps tab says "No domain has a trap address yet, so these settings do nothing." under its Control Deck
  button while no domain has one, and how many have otherwise, the domains counted off the UI thread with "Counting
  the domains that have trap addresses…" in its place meanwhile, so that a server of many domains does not hold the
  page as it opens. On every settings page the sentence after a save names the setting it changed, or counts the
  changes ("Saved 3 changes at 14:20:00 - applied immediately."), or says no setting had changed; a number typed into
  a box is saved as typed when Alt+S presses Save changes with the keyboard still in the box, where the box had not
  yet taken it in and the save wrote the number it held before and said no setting had changed; a save refused over
  the thresholds, from whichever tab it is made, shows the refuse threshold on General - scrolled to, ringed and with
  the keyboard in it - and once they are put right the notice that refused the save goes. `AntiSpamPageTests` holds
  the checks, the sentence and the page's wiring.

- **Fixed: the virus scanning overview froze while it counted every account's fetch accounts, cut its key pill in
  other languages, and said nothing of the sandbox.** The page read everything on the UI thread, the walk of up to
  1,000 accounts for their external POP3 fetch accounts among it - one round trip each - so a large installation's
  window stopped answering, and what showed while it read was the page as it had been; the "On, but cannot run" pill
  was held to 170 pixels and cut in German, French and Russian with no tool tip; the attachment sandbox, which holds
  and quarantines messages for what they carry, was not mentioned; and the verdict counted the scanners and repeated
  the size rule the next card states (review finding F265). The cards are now drawn from the quick reads and the fetch
  accounts counted off the UI thread, "Counting external accounts…" where the count goes, the title's pill saying no
  "No problems found" until the count is in and the keyboard kept where it was when the page is drawn again; a count
  of a page read again or left is dropped. The scanners' pills take their whole words, each as wide as its own word
  where an Off was stretched to the width of the column's longest, and a status pill that its row squeezes says the
  whole word in a tool tip. A card, Attachments opened in a sandbox, says whether the sandbox is on, with a pill and a
  Settings… button that opens the Sandbox tab of Anti-virus settings, and what its verdicts do - delivered when clean,
  quarantined when malicious or returned while quarantining is off, and delivered with a header or returned when no
  verdict comes in time - and switched on with an address empty it is a Warning among the problems. The verdict names
  the scanners in the order they run ("Every message is scanned by two scanners in turn: Custom scanner, then
  ClamAV.") and, with a size limit, says "within the size limit" and leaves the limit to the Warning under it.
  `VirusPipelineTests` and `VirusOverviewPageTests` hold the sentences and the wiring.

- **Fixed: the sign-in card named its act with two verbs, and said only the Administrator signs in on it.** It was
  headed "Connect to server" over "Sign in with the hMailServer administrator credential.", its button said Connect,
  and while it worked it said "Signing in…"; German and Japanese repeated the split (Verbinden and anmelden, 接続 and
  サインイン). The heading and the button now both say Sign in, as the page is named (the owner's choice of 9 October 2026),
  and the card's accessible name is its heading; the pill keeps Connected and Not connected for the link. The subtitle
  says who signs in here - "Sign in as the server's Administrator, or with your own account if it administers a domain
  or holds a role." - and the password's hint which password that is, the one chosen at install for Administrator and
  an account's own for the account, where it named the install's alone. The Welcome page's starting point is "Protect
  the administrator password", the words the card and Administrative access use, where it said credential. Every
  language has the new words, the button's Alt key one the card's other captions leave free. `SignInWordsTests` holds
  the heading, the button, the card's name, the hint and, in every catalogue, the button saying what the heading says.

- **Fixed: the Dashboard and the Setup checklist counted the same states in different words.** The Dashboard's setup
  card said "11 things need attention." and the checklist "11 need action, 1 cannot be told from here, 9 done, 4 not
  needed." - a first clause with no noun - while the pills on both pages said Action needed and Cannot tell. Both now
  read their sentences from one place, `Services/SetupTally`, each state a sentence of its own in the forms its
  language has for the count and in its pill's words: the card "11 items need action. 1 item cannot be checked from
  here." or "Nothing needs action - all 25 external setup checks are done or not needed.", and the checklist "4 items
  need action. 7 items cannot be checked from here. 4 items are not needed. Next step: ...", leaving out a state no
  item is in. `SetupTallyTests` holds the sentences, a Russian count's few and many forms, the German ones in their
  pills' words - "Bei 10 Punkten besteht Handlungsbedarf." beside the pill Handlungsbedarf, where they said "10 Punkte
  erfordern eine Maßnahme." - every language's "Nothing needs action" in one phrase, and both pages reading them.

- **Fixed: three small copy slips - a chart title that said its unit twice, a palette row that told its reader to press
  Ctrl+K, and five field captions that ended in a colon.** The Dashboard's sessions chart was titled "Active sessions
  (sessions)", which Japanese cut to "アクティブなセッション (セッショ…" at 1280; a chart card now shows its unit in brackets only
  where its title does not name it (`ChartDefinition.CardTitle`, the sessions chart marked `TitleNamesUnit`, since
  Finnish counts "istuntoa" in "Aktiiviset istunnot"), and the table and the spoken words keep the unit. The Welcome
  page's purpose, which the Ctrl+K palette shows as its first row and the sidebar as a tool tip, said "or press Ctrl+K
  and describe what you want to do" to a reader already in the palette; it says "or describe what you want to do in the
  search". The DNS records page's "Domain:" and the new public folder's "Folder name:" are "Domain" and "Folder name",
  as every other caption above a field is, the folder's with an Alt key; the second factor's prompt asks for the
  "6-digit code from your authenticator app", where it said "Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app:", and
  the DKIM record of the domain's dialog and the new IMAP folder of the account's end in no colon. `SmallCopyTests`
  holds the titles, that no page's purpose names Ctrl+K, and that no FieldRow caption ends in a colon - a Label set in
  code or in XAML, a caption given to a helper that builds the row, or a text prompt's.

- **Fixed: the Domains & accounts page called one act Properties and Edit, and the dialog its Members button opens said
  recipient.** Domain and distribution list rows carried Properties, account rows and the Groups page Edit, for the
  same act of opening the item's dialog, and each row's button was "Edit" or "Properties" to a screen reader whatever
  row it was on. Every row that opens an editor now says Edit - the domain and account rows' word, the list row's glyph
  a pencil where it was a cog, the rows' menus Edit… - and each button is named for its row, "Edit domain example.com",
  "Edit account ...", "Edit distribution list ...", the name starting with the button's word in every language. The
  page's help, DomainsAndAccounts.md, says Edit on a domain's row and the pencil on a list's, where it said Properties
  and the gear. The members dialog says member throughout: its heading "Members of everyone@example.com" and title
  "Members - ...", its box "Address to add as a member", "Remove the member ... from this list?", "No members yet,
  ...", "2 members added." and its failures, where each said recipient. French, Italian and Russian give Members… an
  Alt key of its own (Mem_bres, Mem_bri, Уча_стники), where it took the M of Modifier and Modifica and the У of Удалить
  beside it, on the list's menu and on the Groups page. `DomainsVerbWordsTests` holds the rows, their names and
  Members…' keys in every catalogue, the dialog's words and the help's; `DomainsFormsTests` and `DomainsRowVerbsTests`
  hold the new names and menus.

- **Fixed: the Administrator roles page left the built-in roles' purposes in English, said its subtitle twice, and gave
  its form no examples.** "What it is for" showed the description hm_roles holds, which the database scripts write in
  English, so German and Japanese read "Every permission, in every domain." among translated captions; it is now each
  built-in role's purpose from the catalogue, by the role's name (`Services/RoleWords`), and a custom role's as typed.
  The subtitle is one sentence - "Who may administer what: the roles this server has, and the accounts that hold
  them." - and the built-in roles and what an account without a role holds are said on the Roles card, where the empty
  state said the second again; it is now "Nobody has been given a role yet.". Built in reads Yes or No, where a custom
  role's cell was empty, and an assignment's domains "example.com, example.net", where they were run together. The
  form's placeholders are examples, helpdesk@example.com and example.com, example.net, where they said the captions
  again; the Domains box says what empty gives - the account's own domain, or every domain for serveradmin and auditor,
  and * every domain for any role - and what is typed there is sent trimmed. Give the role and Take the role away stand
  on the boxes' line whatever a box's hint adds under it. `RoleWordsTests` holds the purposes to the scripts' own words
  and to every catalogue, the domains as shown and as sent, and the page's words and form.

- **Fixed: the Domains & accounts page said two failures as "Couldn't load ...", and its Create account said a lost
  link as the runtime's text.** The aliases' and distribution lists' read failures began "Couldn't load aliases: " and
  "Couldn't load distribution lists: " beside "Could not read the domains: " and "Could not read the accounts: "; they
  now say "Could not read the aliases: " and "Could not read the distribution lists: ". Create account gave the
  server's reason through the catalogue but showed a lost link as "The RPC server is unavailable. (0x800706BA)", where
  the page's other handlers said the link but the server's words untranslated; every failure on the Domains and Public
  folders pages now gives its reason through `ServerSession.DescribeComError`, which says a sentence of the server's
  own that the catalogue holds - a breached password, a breach check that could not run - in the reader's language, on
  every page that says a failure. `DomainsFailureWordsTests` holds the prefixes, the handlers and DescribeComError's
  catalogue.

- **Fixed: the hMailServer.ini pages spelt the file two ways, Directory authentication captioned its fields with their
  keys, and example placeholders read as values.** Subtitles, card blurbs, the buttons' help and the notices said
  "hMailServer.INI" above a line that said "Editing C:\...\hMailServer.ini", the file's own name as the server makes
  it; every text, message, search alias and path now says hMailServer.ini. Directory authentication (LDAP)'s captions
  carried their keys in brackets - "Directory server host name (Server)", "Use LDAP directory authentication
  (Enabled)", in Japanese and Chinese with the Alt key after the bracket - and its state card listed keys, "the
  section is also missing: Server, SearchBase (or UserDnTemplate, to bind directly without searching)". The captions
  are plain, each field's hint ends with the key, "Stored as [LDAP] Server.", the card says what is missing in a whole
  sentence by the fields' captions, "Before enabling, fill in Directory server host name.", and the texts that named a
  key - "AllowUnprotectedPassword is off", "set ServiceUsername", "make UserSearchFilter or SearchBase select exactly
  one entry" - name the field. The page's example placeholders and the Authentication page's token issuer say they are
  examples, "e.g. dc01.example.local", where in the light theme they read as values, the host name's directly under
  the notice that it was missing; Directory synchronisation's attribute boxes and its entry ceiling say in their hints
  the default an empty box stands for, as well as in grey. `IniPagesWordingTests` holds the file's name in every text
  and string, the captions, the keys in the hints, the missing sentences and the placeholders, and
  `SettingNamesInTextTests` reads the two [LDAP] pages' keys.

- **Fixed: three hints carried an aside or the project's history.** Directory authentication (LDAP)'s connection test
  began its last sentence "One honest caveat:", Directory synchronisation called bringing one domain over at a time
  "the sane way to do this the first time", and the archive retention on the Protocols page's SMTP tab said that
  "until now nothing ever removed anything from it" and that the administrator who found out was "the one whose disk
  filled up" - words every translator had to recreate and that told the administrator nothing. They now read "Note:
  the test runs from this computer, ...", "The first time, bring one domain over at a time." and "The archive folder
  is a raw copy of every message that passes through the server, so on a busy server it is a directory that only
  grows; this prunes it.", in every language; the Auto-ban tarpit's history of TarpitDelay had gone with the copy
  pass. `HintAsidesTests` holds the catalogue to none of the asides.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel called signing in by eight names, and one setting a relayer, a relay and a smart host.**
  The group called Sign-in & access said "keeps failing to log on", "Max invalid logon attempts", "Logon tarpit",
  "Delay per failed logon", "Minimum seconds between logins" and "log on with their domain password" beside webmail
  texts that said sign in. Every text now says sign in for the act and sign-in for the noun, for people and mail
  clients alike, and logon only for Windows - Windows logon, LogonUser, an account's logon restrictions, the service's
  Log on as a service right; the Auto-ban captions read "Failed sign-ins before an address is banned (0 = off)",
  "Sign-in tarpit" and "Delay per failed sign-in (seconds; 0 = off)" - the first, in German and Dutch, "bevor eine
  Adresse gebannt wird" and "voordat een adres wordt verbannen", a ban as each of their other ban texts says it - and
  Japanese says サインイン and Brazilian Portuguese login wherever the English says sign in. The glossary the review
  asked for is a section of
  docs/ControlPanelDesign.md, Words, and applied in one pass: the Delivery of e-mail page's Relayer tab and its SMTP
  relayer (smart host) card are Smart host and Server-wide smart host, and the tab's captions and OAuth2 card, the
  page's subtitle and description and the Routes page's empty state say smart host as well - "Smart host name (empty =
  direct delivery)", "The smart host requires authentication", "OAuth2 for the smart host (Microsoft 365)", "Outbound
  delivery, retries and the smart host." - where they said relay host, relay and smart-host relaying, as the domain
  dialog's relay host, its hint and the stored-secrets note say, and the palette still finds the page by SMTP relayer
  and Relay host; e-mail is mail in prose and email address for the field ("Email" in the Active Directory picker);
  Couldn't is Could not, client id and key id are client ID and key ID, the nine texts that wrote a server error's
  number as "(error 5921)", "error HM5113", "the server logs error 5113" or "the server reports HM5508" say "server
  error" before it, "(server error 5921)", "server error 5113", the TCP/IP ports grid's Security column is Connection
  security, and three captions lose the colon at their end (the public folder's name, the code the second factor asks
  for, the DKIM record). The SSL certificates and SSL/TLS pages keep their titles until the page names are decided
  again, as Delivery of e-mail does, and the glossary says so beside its TLS for prose, which every other text already
  says. `GlossaryTests` holds the English to the glossary - a server error's number in any of those
  forms, Windows' own error 1069 apart - the smart host to its name on its tab, in the search index and wherever a
  text sends the reader to it, SSL to the two pages' titles and OpenSSL, the Brazilian catalogue to login, and every
  caption to no colon.

- **Fixed: the dialogs' captions carried their whole explanation in brackets, which a screen reader heard as the field's
  name.** "Address (changing it renames the mailbox; it must stay in this domain)", "Delete
  messages in this domain's mailboxes older than (days; 0 = no policy, an account's own value overrides it)", "Warning
