  text (empty = the server message; %MACRO_MAILBOX%, ...)", the restricted delivery's named domains and the
  impersonation tab's protected persons and partners with a sentence each - the caption is the editor's accessible
  name. A caption now names the field and, in its brackets, the unit, the range and what an edge value means, and the
  rest is the field's hint under the box, which is its help text too: "Address" with "Changing it renames the mailbox;
  it must stay in this domain.", "Warning text (empty = the server message)" with "It may use %MACRO_MAILBOX%,
  %MACRO_QUOTA%, %MACRO_USED% and %MACRO_PERCENT%." - which four catalogues had written without their underscores, the
  Alt-key mark, and now spell as the server reads them. Eighteen captions of the domain, account and external account
  dialogs - "Domain name (changing it renames the domain and moves every account, alias and list with it)",
  "Restricted delivery (the named domains are on the domain's dialog)" among them - and eleven of the IP range, mailbox
  move, rule action and TCP/IP port dialogs and the list editors' dialogs - "Priority (higher wins when ranges
  overlap)", "SSL certificate (required for SSL/TLS and STARTTLS)", "Mirror every folder (IMAP only: a migration,
  verbatim, with flags and dates)" - in every language. A hint that is an example says so in a sentence, "For example
  allow:GB,IE or block:CN,RU." under the country policy and "For example partner.example, or .example for the domain
  and everything beneath it; ..." under the named domains, where each was the bare example, and so does the external
  process timeout's, "For example a command-line virus scanner.". `CaptionWordingTests` holds every caption of the
  dialogs to the rule: a part of a bracket with a ";" or an "=" in it is a unit, a range or what values mean, each
  meaning five words at most, and a bracket with neither is a unit, a range, "optional", "leave empty to keep current"
  or three words at most; and every hint of the dialogs to begin as a sentence does.

- **Fixed: field captions said a unit, a range and what 0 means in a dozen ways, and one said 0 meant "default" where
  it means every host.** The Anti-spam and Anti-virus pages alone had "(KB, 0 = unlimited)", "(0 never refuses)",
  "Record expiration interval, minutes", "(0-100)" and "Minutes the sending address is banned (0 = no ban; up to
  525600)", with "Max" and "Maximum" in one card; the settings pages added "(s)", "in seconds", "N days", "0 =
  disabled", "0 = no bound", "0 = keep", "Domain cache max size", "(empty asks the domain's MX hosts)", "(leave it
  empty for one named after today's date)" and numbers without their thousands separated. Every caption now says them
  one way: "<what> (<unit>, <range>; 0 = <meaning>)" - "Ban the sending address for (minutes, up to 525,600; 0 = no
  ban)", "Largest message to spam-scan (KB; 0 = no limit)", "SMTP server minimum timeout (seconds)", "Domain cache
  maximum size (KB, resets at service restart)" - with "no limit", "off", "for ever" and "no time limit" for what 0
  means and "empty = ..." for what an empty box does, "Selector for the new key (empty = today's date)", and the
  explanations these captions carried in their brackets are now their settings' hints. The quarantine digest's address
  is "Release link address", with "Such as https://mail.example.com. Leave empty to send no digest." under it. The
  four timeouts of Server limits & expert settings that did not say what 0 means, and its reserved threads, now do.
  "Extra delivery attempts per additional MX host (0 = default)" is "MX hosts tried per attempt, times the attempt
  number (0 = all)": the setting bounds how many of a domain's MX hosts each attempt tries, and its hint had said it
  multiplied the retry count. The hints group their thousands as the captions above them do and no longer repeat the
  range a caption gives - "The default, 604,800, is a week; 86,400 is a day and 31,557,600 a year, the longest RFC 8461
  allows." under "Policy max age (seconds, 86,400 to 31,557,600)", where it said "From 86400, a day, to 31557600, a
  year" - and so do the other hints and messages that wrote a quantity ungrouped, "At most 2,592,000, thirty days.",
  "Enter a number of days from 0 (for ever) to 3,650.". About 170 captions and hints, in every language, each with its
  own grouping, "2.592.000", "2 592 000"; the Russian, which wrote what 0 means as
  "(0 — без ограничения)" in 29 captions and "(0 = ...)" in 85, and the Ukrainian once, write "=" as the English and
  the other catalogues do, and both name a caption's unit in one case, "(дни; 0 = никогда)" where it was "(дней; 0 —
  никогда)" beside "(дни, до 3 650; ...)". `CaptionFormTests` holds every caption of the Control Panel to the form -
  "max" in either case, but MTA-STS's own max age, and what an empty box means in prose, in a caption or an input
  prompt's - every catalogue to the English's "<n> =", and every English text to a quantity's grouped thousands.

- **Fixed: about sixty texts wrote a word in capitals to stress it, and a few said "honestly" or "perfectly".** "This
  server only CHECKS SPF on incoming mail", "the PTR is NOT published in your domain's zone", "applied to THIS
  account's copy", "Where mail FROM this domain leaves through", "Match ALL criteria (AND)", "Replace ALL configured
  ports", "READ THIS FIRST:", "Applied when a password is CHOSEN", "The directory ACCEPTED the credentials", "Signing
  is currently ON." - and the catalogues copied the capitals, "den RICHTIGEN Schlüssel", "LESEN SIE DAS ZUERST",
  「正しい」パスフレーズ. Every one is written in sentence case, in every language, and the sentence carries the stress:
  "One notice, not one per message", "0 does not mean no time limit." where it was "0 is NOT no bound.", "every
  connection appears to come from that device" where it was "from IT". "Not checked from here, honestly", "can
  honestly be offered", "the honest response", "it will validate perfectly" and "That is deliberate, not a bug" lose
  the word that told the administrator nothing, "many spray sources live behind it" is "many bulk senders hide behind
  it", the quota warning's hint loses its two sentences about what the server did before, and the password expiry's
  hint begins with what it says, where it began "READ THIS FIRST:" under a card that already says to read it.
  `EmphasisCapitalsTests` holds the English and every catalogue to no word in capitals but a name - a protocol, a
  command, a record type, a unit, the rule editor's operators and its IF and THEN.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel spelt some of its English the American way, beside the British of the same pages.** The
  Delivery of e-mail subtitle said "behavior", Transport security "Honor recipient DANE/TLSA records" and "Honor
  recipient MTA-STS policies", "Organization name in TLS reports" and in DMARC reports, Anti-spam "Find organizational
  domains by DNS tree walk", SSL/TLS "Prioritize ChaCha20-Poly1305", Hardening and the stalled-mail guide "Message
  finalization deadline", Webmail's import "Google authorization endpoint", and About "modernizes", where the same
  pages say behaviour, honour, organisation and synchronisation (review finding F298). Each is now British -

  all seventeen catalogues with their translations unchanged, and the settings search index with them; the server's
  own names (the setting keys, the HTTP header Authorization:) keep their spelling, and Ctrl+K finds a setting typed
  either way ("honor dane", "organization name"). `BritishSpellingTests` reads every English text for an American
  form.

- **Fixed: the Japanese Control Panel said one thing in several words, spaced sixteen access keys apart from their
  captions and mixed full-width parentheses into half-width ones.** A key was キー on the REST API keys page and 鍵 for a
  DKIM or TLS key (251 times); an auto-ban was 自動ブロック in the page's title and its settings, 自動 BAN, BAN, 禁止 and 遮断 in
  their text; one paragraph of the sender lists said 差出人 and 送信者, 迷惑メール and スパム; the Logging page and its tab were ログ,
  a log; Server status's Started said 開始済み, "begun"; the TLS overview's Opportunistic said 日和見的; and a route's target
  host was 宛先 beside 送信先 for its port (review finding F302). The catalogue now has a style note at its head, and
  follows it: キー for every key (公開キー, 秘密キー, キー ファイル); 自動 BAN for the feature and its page and BAN for a ban; 送信者 for
  the sender, with 差出人 kept for the From header, and スパム; ログ設定, 開始日時, 日和見暗号化 and 送信先 SMTP ホスト; half-width parentheses
  throughout; and a caption's key suffix written against it, サンプルドメインを作成(_D), as the 531 others are - in the Chinese
  catalogue too, which had the same sixteen - and at its end, after a parenthesis the caption ends with, 宛先フォルダー
  (サーバー上)(_F), as 95 are, where ten stood before the parenthesis. Four texts no access key reaches - the SSL/TLS
  page's TLS 1.3 suites, Diagnostics' message store scan, the Setup checklist's DKIM step and the anti-spam page's spamd
  user - wrote TLSAES_256_GCM_SHA384, hmailservermessagestore_missing_files, `<selector>.domainkey.<domain>` and
  userprefs and ended in a stray "(_A)", "(_M)", "(_D)" and "(_P)", the loss of an underscore read as an Alt key, the
  third telling an administrator to publish the DKIM record at the wrong name; they write the names as the English
  does. The Danish, Finnish, Norwegian and Polish quota warning's caption wrote %MACROMAILBOX%, %MACROQUOTA%,
  %MACROUSED% and %MACROPERCENT%, names the server does not substitute - WPF takes only a caption's first underscore
  for its key and shows the rest - and writes %MACRO_MAILBOX% and the three others as the English does. Every text that
  names the two renamed pages names them by their new titles. `JapaneseStyleTests` holds the note,
  `CatalogueIdentifierTests` every name with an underscore in every language - two underscores or more, a server macro,
  a DNS label such as ._domainkey. or _dmarc., a snake_case name in a sentence - and no Japanese or Chinese key suffix
  on a text whose English has no access key, and `build/check-mnemonics.py` refuses a space before a Japanese or
  Chinese key's suffix, its self-test with a catalogue made to break it.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel's examples were in some captions and in other boxes, said yourdomain.com, could read as
  values already set, and were faint in the dark theme.** Routes said "Domain (e.g. partner.com)", IP ranges "Lower IP
  (e.g. 10.0.0.0)" and "Upper IP (e.g. 10.0.0.255)", the rule dialogs "Header name (e.g. X-Spam-Status)" and "IMAP
  folder (e.g. INBOX.Archive)", MX query "Domain (e.g. gmail.com)" and a domain's aliases "Alias domain name (e.g.
  example.net)", each its whole example in the field's accessible name, while other pages put theirs in the box;
  Transport security, Certificates (ACME), Web services, Server sendout and the setup checklist's ACME item said
  yourdomain.com where the rest say example.com, and the translations invented their own (mail.ihredomain.de,
  mail.dindomän.se); an empty DNS override showed 1.1.1.1, which read as a Cloudflare resolver set on this server, and
  an empty REST API port 8045 and OpenTelemetry endpoint http://localhost:4318 as values configured; "e.g. 127.0.0.1"
  was English in every language; and a dark placeholder on a card's field measured 4.36:1 (review findings F303,
  F099). Each caption now names its field and its box shows the example marked as one - "e.g. partner.example", "e.g.
  1.1.1.1", "e.g. mail.example.com" - in every language (z. B., p. ex., 例:), or, in a dialog whose boxes have no
  placeholder and in a list's dialog, its hint under the box says it ("Such as X-Spam-Status"); the examples are from
  example.com and example.net, MX query's gmail.com excepted, since example.com publishes no mail server; the
  sendout's From name says what it is under the box rather than inside it. The dark theme's tertiary text and
  placeholders are white at 60% (`DesignTokens.DarkTertiaryText`), 5.3:1 on a field's fill on a card and 6.7:1 on the
  page, published under both keys Wpf.Ui's text fields read. `PlaceholderExampleTests` holds the captions, the boxes
  and yourdomain's absence, and `DesignTokensTests` the dark text on every dark surface a field or a hint sits on.

- **Fixed: small copy and layout defects, page by page.** DNS records: one caption said two things, "Record type: MX.

  someone@example.com", "Move to folder 'Invoices'", "Set header X-Rule to (empty)" - where the list said "Forward
  e-mail -> someone@example.com", "Move to IMAP folder 'Invoices'" and "Set header value X-Rule=", three ways in one
  list, and a criterion is one whole text a language can order; the criteria's card is titled IF, level with THEN,

  Delivery, retries and throttling; the reputation watch quotes its alert's identifier, "raises the alert

  was below the fold; four SMTP settings' blurbs of six and seven lines say what the setting does in two sentences,

  "Changes apply after pressing Save" names the button as it is captioned, Save changes (F310). SSL certificates,
  SSL/TLS, Transport security and the IP range dialog: the apply marks say "Applies on save", "Applies after a
  reinitialise" and "Applies after a restart", where the last two said "After reinitialise" and "After a restart";
  SSL/TLS's tab is named Ciphers & verification, as its card is (German Cipher-Suiten und Prüfung, where it left
  "Ciphers" untranslated); the IP range's four directions say Local to local and so on under the caption that says
  they require authentication, which is each box's help text, where each said "Require auth:" again; Transport
  security's trust anchors are captioned "Trust anchors (DS records, separated by semicolons)" with the format and the
  IANA root's KSK-2017 as an example under the box, where the caption was the format string; a certificate's details
  say only what the word beside each does not - the date in the word, what follows in the sentence - where "Valid
  until 2027-01-09 (90 days left)" stood beside "... is valid until 2027-01-09, 90 days from now"; the status columns
  are Certificate status and Key status, where Certificate and Private key read as repeats of the file columns; and
  the page loads under "Checking the certificate files…" (F311). The auto-ban captions the finding names are left to
  T3.1 item 9 (F143), which puts them in the sign-in vocabulary. Spam and virus: each scanner has one name on its
  settings tab and on the virus scanning overview - ClamWin, Custom scanner, ClamAV (clamd) - where ClamAV was "ClamAV
  (network daemon)" on one and "ClamAV (clamd, over TCP)" on the other and the custom scanner had three names; its
  result is "Exit code that means infected"; the notices are Notify the sender and Notify the recipients; the
  scanners' tabs are in the order the server runs them, ClamWin, Custom scanner, ClamAV; greylisting's MX switch says
  what it does, "Skip greylisting when the connecting address is an A or MX host of the sender's domain", and the
  bypass list says Matched on and HELO name as the overview does; the virus overview's subtitle says "a message found
  to be infected" where it was "condemned", and its card is Attachment blocking; and a settings button's failure names

  its subtitle and every catalogue call it, and Journaling and dual delivery is Journaling & dual delivery, as the

- **Fixed: file pickers, the administrators' signposts, repeated wording and the dialogs' headings.** A file picker on

  Administrator roles among its related pages for an administrator who may open it (review finding F324). Texts that

  failure is the overviews' sentence; Directory synchronisation's save and restart messages are the LDAP page's, which

- **Fixed: About promised support it did not give, the help pane listed every document in one run, and the design
  document's frame was out of date.** About opens on Get help - the forum, the issue tracker, the source code and Copy
  version details, which puts the Control Panel's version and build, the server's version and host, the database, .NET
  and Windows on the clipboard, in English, for a report - then the versions as a label and a value a line with the
  licence, Connected to and the report's server line keeping the host when the server does not give its version,
  "Server: hMailServer (version not read) on mail.example.com" - then who maintains it, the name in ordinary strong
  text; it promised "where to get support" with no forum, no issue tracker and nothing to copy, set the developer's name
  larger than the product's, and read as a brochure ("A modern administration app", "re-armed with modern
  cryptography"), where its words now say what is so (review finding F314, and the owner's choice of 9 October 2026).
  The help pane's list of every document is grouped as the sidebar is - under each group the documents its pages and
  their tabs open - then Reference and Building and packaging, each by title, the project's pipelines, environments and
  packages under the last, the snap with the Nix flake and Alpine, where some 120 documents stood in one run with
  ContinuousIntegration, Fuzzing and Nix among the operators' guides; while the list shows, its search box says Search
  all documentation and narrows the list to the documents whose title or text holds the words, the line under it saying
  how many do - "3 documents contain "DNSSEC"." - or that none does, to a screen reader as well, and Enter opening the
  first once two characters narrow the list, where it said Search this document and searched the list's own words; and
  Back, at the head of the pane, returns to what a link in it left, and hands the keyboard to the search box when it
  goes with nothing left to go back to. docs/ControlPanelDesign.md's frame describes the window's four rows, the help
  pane and the pending bar, and names the two renamed groups by their old names and their new ones, and the
  account-rules list editor nothing built, whose subtitle said a rule's criteria could not be edited here, is gone with
  its seven texts (F315). `AboutPageTests` and `HelpDocumentListTests` hold it.

- **Fixed: the help pane's list of documents was justified.** All documentation, and the list a page without a guide
  shows, spread a wrapped title's words across the pane ("Account  recovery:  a  recovery  address  and  one-time")
  while the documents beside them were ragged right, and the line that says a document is not in this copy was in the
  viewer's own face and size. Every document the pane shows - the ones it renders and the ones it writes itself - now
  starts from one document in the pane's face, size and colour, ragged right and unhyphenated
  (`MarkdownFlow.NewDocument`). `HelpDocumentTypographyTests` holds it.

- **Fixed: German quotations closed with a straight typewriter quote.** 83 German texts opened a quotation with „
  and closed it with ", so the palette's placeholder read „Spam stoppen", DNS records „v=DMARC1" and the setup
  checklist „Prüfen", beside „Sicherung jetzt starten“ closed properly elsewhere. Every German quotation now closes
  with “, and `build/check-catalogues.py` holds the German, Czech and Polish catalogues to quotations closed by their
  language's own mark before the next one opens.

  sizes.** The Dashboard's "Setup checklist…", DNS records' "Open Domains…", "Host name setting…" and "PTR / HELO
  checks…", the transport encryption and virus scanning overviews' "Ports…", "Certificates…", "Settings…" and
  "Patterns…", Directory authentication's "Open Domains..." and "Open Live logs...", REST API keys' "REST listener
  settings…", the settings pages' signposts' "Open…" and the SSL certificates page's "Set up ACME…" opened a page and

  ports' Properties, which open a dialog, had no ellipsis - IP ranges' Properties, on a list page made the same way,
  had one. Each link now names the page it opens without one - "Open Setup checklist", "Open Domains", "Open Protocols
  (host name)", "SSL/TLS →" as the spam filtering overview already wrote it - and the list editor's and the
  permissions dialog's buttons are "Add…" and "Edit…", and the three list pages' "Properties…", with IP ranges' access
  key. The links in a card are one style, `CompactPageLink` (the Caption size, 28 pixels tall at the least), where
  seven pages drew their own 24-pixel links beside the card's 32-pixel buttons, and a caption with an access key is
  that size too: the Dashboard's "Open Setup checklist" was drawn at 14 pixels, the Body size WPF-UI's style gives the
  text of an access key over the button's own. An arrow link's accessible name is its words without the arrow,
  "Blocked senders: Open Blocked senders, which owns the Blocked senders settings", where a screen reader read the
  arrow and a colon after it in the middle of the name. The Dashboard's Uptime is the 28 pixels of the other four
  figures, where it was 20, each figure shrinks only when it is wider than its card (at 760 pixels "128,431" was cut
  to "128,43"), and the labels under them are the Caption size, where they were 11 pixels, and wrap where the card is
  narrower than they are. `NavigationCaptionTests` holds the captions, every XAML button that opens a dialog for input
  among them, the style and the figures, and `LabelInNameTests` the arrow links' names.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel wrote three dashes and two ellipses, sometimes two of them in one sentence.** Most texts
  used the spaced hyphen, but 21 used an em dash and 3 an en dash ("Public — anyone can send" beside "Nobody - the
  members are added here"; "That may well be deliberate - the suggestion ... Published: {0} — just confirm"), the
  code joined a state word, a certificate's name and a folder permission with " — ", and captions and progress words
  ended in three dots ("Applying...", "C_hoose a photo...", "Restarting the hMailServer service...") beside the
  ellipsis character ("Saving…"). Every text now writes the spaced hyphen - the owner's choice - and every caption
  that opens a dialog, progress word and unfinished list the ellipsis character; three dots stay only for omitted
  literal text (p=..., https://host/...). The two "...within (minutes)" captions of Auto-ban are worded whole
  ("Failures counted within (minutes)", "Failures for a name counted within (minutes)"), "two, four, six...
  seconds" says "and so on", the generated password's toast reads "copied to the clipboard; reveal it with the eye
  icon", texts padded with spaces for an alignment the layout never kept ("Version {0}  -  .NET {1}", and the
  domain dialog's DKIM record, "Type:       TXT" under "Host/Name:  {0}", which lined up in no translation) and
  Directory synchronisation's preview, which joined "jane.doe@example.com  -  create" and "1  -  the entry has no mail
  attribute" in code, have single spaces, and the one date format written in lower case is "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" as
  the others are. Each change is made in the seventeen translations, and their own dashes follow the same rule: the
  hyphen, but for Russian and Ukrainian (the em dash) and Czech (the en dash), whose typography and catalogues write a
  dash of their own, one kind to a text, and a range written "1-14". `build/check-catalogues.py` holds the English to
  no em or en dash and three dots only for literal text, each translation to its catalogue's dash and to three dots
  only where its English has them, and every text to no padding; `PaddedJoinTests` holds the code's own joins to it,
  and `docs/ControlPanelDesign.md` states the rule.

- **Fixed: cipher lists, LDAP names, log lines, the bearer header and paths were set in the UI face, and monospaced
  text came in three sizes.** The SSL/TLS page's cipher list, TLS 1.3 suites and key exchange groups and Directory
  authentication's search base and DN template were Segoe text boxes; the transport encryption overview's "Cipher
  list for TLS 1.2 and below: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:..." was caption prose that broke inside a suite name;
  REST API keys marked off "Authorization: Bearer hmapi_..." by two spaces inside its sentence and wrapped the key
  store's path at a backslash; and the stalled-mail guide's log lines were body text in SemiBold. Each is in the
  monospaced face now - the overview's list a run of its own that breaks only after a colon, the header on a line of
  its own, the store's path cut in its middle with the whole of it in the tool tip, the guide's log words
  (SpamTestSpamAssassin, Time:, done spam-protection, 451 4.3.1) runs of their own in each row's sentence, whose other
  words, such as "with a large", "slow" and "then silence", stay in the body face - and every box and block of
  monospaced text is one size, the new `AppFontSizeMono` (13), where the live log was 12, the diagnostics 12, the DNS
  record and DKIM boxes 12, the help pane's code blocks 12, and the event script, the TOTP setup key, the generated
  password, the quarantine's headers and a setting's name 14; the one-time code boxes stay 28 pixels, for six digits
  typed off a phone. `MonospacedDataTests` holds the faces, the size at every site of the face in the Control Panel's
  sources, and the runs.

- **Changed: REST API keys is under Sign-in & access.** It was the last row of Monitoring & troubleshooting, a group
  whose purpose - "Is mail flowing, and if it is not, where has it stopped?" - says nothing of credentials; a key is a
  credential that is not the administrator password, and the page now follows Administrative access, the page its
  Related links already paired it with. Its key is unchanged, so the palette, the Related links, the tours and every

  groups the review proposed beside it each add a rail glyph and wait on the owner's decision. `SidebarStructureTests`
  holds the place.

- **Fixed: a text box that wraps justified its lines.** WPF-UI's styles stretch a text box's content, which WPF's text
  box reads as justified text, so every wrapped line of an account's or a domain's signature and auto-reply, a rule's
  reply and disclaimer, a distribution list's footer, a server message or an LDAP filter was spread to the box's width
  as it was typed ("message  when  I  am  back."), and the domain dialog's DKIM record wrote "Value:", "v=DKIM1;" and
  "k=rsa;" at the box's left, middle and right above the key. The implicit text box styles in `App.xaml`, WPF's and
  WPF-UI's, set a box that wraps ragged right; a one-line box keeps WPF-UI's alignment. `docs/ControlPanelDesign.md`
  states the rule beside the help pane's, and `RaggedRightTextBoxTests` holds both styles and refuses a box that wraps
  and sets its own alignment.

- **Fixed: the SSL certificates page and Directory synchronisation drew two filled accent buttons on one screen, and
  the passphrase box was as wide as its placeholder.** With a certificate selected, Save passphrase on its details
  card and Add on the add form were both Primary, beside the red Delete selected, and Directory synchronisation's
  Preview was Primary under the header's Save changes, so that each page showed two buttons that looked like its one
  way on; the details card's New passphrase box was 151 pixels wide, its placeholder's width, and grew as a passphrase
  was typed (review finding F140). Save passphrase, Preview and Save and preview are secondary buttons, so that the
  add form's Add and the header's Save changes are each page's one Primary, and the passphrase box is 360 pixels wide
  whatever it holds. `OnePrimaryPerScreenTests` holds both pages to one Primary and the box to its width.

- **Fixed: the transport encryption overview's certificate rows were laid out unlike its listener rows, and a status
  mark at the level that says nothing was drawn in the primary text colour.** Each certificate row put a pill with the
  level's word, "OK" or "Warning", on the left before a run-on of the name, the finding and the use - "wildcard-2025
  (moved to the old disk) — The certificate file does not exist on this machine ... mail on those ports stops., not
  used by any listener" - where the listener rows above it have the name on the left, the sentence in the middle and
  the state in a pill of its own words on the right (review finding F326). The certificate rows are laid out the same
  way now: the name, with "In use by a listener" or "Not used by any listener" under it; the sentence, "Expires in 60
  days.", "Expired 13 days ago.", "Becomes valid in 5 days." or the SSL certificates page's own sentence for a problem
  with the files; and a pill that says Valid, Expires soon, Has expired, Not valid yet, the problem's word ("File
  missing") or Not checked, at the level the page's notes give the same certificate. A certificate past its date is
  read as expired and not as a problem with its files: taken from the certificates page's finding on its file, its
  pill said that page's "Expired on 2026-09-27 (13 days ago)", an ISO date cut short in German, beside that page's
  long sentence, and the note on one in use said it "has a problem:" before the same sentence
  (`TlsPosture.TakeInspection`); and a certificate whose date of validity is still to come, which clients refuse until
  then, is Not valid yet, with a note, a Warning while a listener uses it as that page's finding is, where it said
  Valid beside that page's Warning. The Normal level's colour is the neutral grey (`StatusSemantics`), where it was
  the primary text, so that the certificate details' "No passphrase needed" mark was a black dot in the light theme
  and a white one in the dark; a mark beside its word takes the level's fill-text shade at every other level, as the
  word does (`StatusPresentation.MarkBrushKey`), and the dashboard's queue length keeps the ordinary text colour while
  the queue is normal. The never-ban list's empty state and the IP ranges page's empty state at its floor, which the
  review saw as column headers with no sentence and a glyph against the header rule, were put right with the empty
  states' work (F207) and are as they should be. `TlsCertificateRowTests` and `StatusSemanticsTests` hold the rows,
  their levels against the notes, certificates written to files and read as the page reads them, and the neutral mark.

- **Fixed: a check box stood ten pixels right of the column its card's captions, boxes and hints share, and the lines
  under it aligned with neither the box nor its caption.** WPF-UI's padding is the box's margin, so that the square
  stood at 336 pixels against 325 for every caption, text box and hint of a settings card, and at 35 against 25 in a
  dialog; a hint under a box began at the row's edge; Back up messages' two options on the backup page stood 22 pixels
  in, under neither its box nor its caption; and on the IP ranges page a permission whose caption wrapped pushed the
  other boxes of its row off their line (review finding F294). Every check box stands on the text column, its caption
  at the top beside it; the hint, the Applies line and the message under a box start under its caption, 28 pixels in -
  the box and its gap - as a dialog's note laid under one does, and so do Directory synchronisation's note on marking
  accounts inactive and a setting level's own value; the backup page's two options stand under Back up messages'
  caption, their notes under their own; and the IP ranges page's permission boxes keep to the top of their row.
  `CheckBoxColumnTests` holds the style, the inset and each of the pages.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel drew three blues, and its primary buttons and ticked boxes took the Windows accent.** The
  selected tab's underline and the title bar's glyph were App.xaml's BrandBrush, #2F81F7 in both themes, whose
  recolour for the theme never took effect; the rail and the selection pills were the brand, #2F6FE0 in the light
  theme and #4C8DFF in the dark; and the primary buttons, the ticked check boxes, the switches and the progress ring
  took the Windows accent, which on a machine whose accent is red or orange is a colour the Control Panel keeps for
  danger and warning (review finding F045). The brand is WPF-UI's accent now, given to it after every theme change, so
  that a primary button, a ticked box, a radio button, a switch, the ring and a text selection are the brand whatever
  accent Windows has, as the owner chose on 9 October 2026; the light theme's primary button keeps its white words at
  4.5:1 or more under the pointer and pressed, where WPF-UI's own, the brand made translucent, measured 4.0:1. The tab
  underline and the title glyph are the brand too, and BrandBrush is gone; under High Contrast the accent is the
  user's. `BrandAccentTests` holds the accent to the brand, the words on it, the theme change and the two blues that
  were left.

- **Fixed: the keyboard's focus was drawn four ways, the breadcrumb and the Related links read as chips, a one-line
  message box was a block of tint 200 pixels tall, and icon sizes had no token.** The text fields drew a violet ring,
  the navigation's rows a violet border, the grids and the tabs a black and white ring, and every WPF-UI control - its
  buttons and check boxes - a one-pixel rectangle in the text colour; WPF-UI's Transparent buttons kept their outline,
  so that the trail, the Related links and the command bar's buttons were a row of boxes; a message box was at least
  320 pixels tall, its notice stretched down it, a question had no mark, and Close was the primary button in one
  dialog and a secondary one in others; and glyphs ran from 12 to 40 pixels with no size of their own (review findings
  F296 and F041). Every control now draws one ring, the focus colour two pixels wide, outside a button, a check box or
  a grid's cell and inside a tab and a navigation or list row, with the black and white ring under High Contrast
  alone; the trail's Back, Forward and groups, the Related links and the command bar's buttons have nothing round them
  at rest, nor while they are disabled (`SubtleButton`); a message box is as tall as its message, its notice at the
  top, a question marked as a notice at the level that says nothing; a dialog whose footer holds Close alone draws it
  as its one primary button; and icons take four sizes, 16, 20, 24 and 40 (`AppIconSizeSm` to `AppIconSizeXl`).
  `FocusRingAndButtonsTests` holds each.

- **Fixed: the Control Panel's spacing was off its own scale, its list cards, dialogs and page columns each named a
  size of their own, and a settings page's cards ended at a different edge on every tab.** A page's padding
  (24,20,24,24) and a card's (20,16) stood on a seventh step, 20, and a dialog's inset was 24,20; the scale's six
  steps were declared in XAML, where no margin could take them and none did; a card's description and footer and a
  settings section's gaps were 10 and 2 pixels; a card holding a list or a grid was padded 4, 6, 8, 10 or 12 by page;
  every dialog named a width - 400, 460, 480, 520, 560, 600, 620, 680, 760; a page's column was 680, 760, 860, 880,
  980 or 1000 pixels; a settings panel was as wide as its widest card, so that the cards' right edges ran from 526 to
  761 pixels tab by tab; and four App.xaml styles had no use (review finding F295). A page's padding and a card's are
  the Control Deck's now, 24 and 16 by 24, a dialog's inset 24, the scaffold's gaps on the scale; a list card takes
  `AppListCardPadding` (8), a dialog a width `DesignTokens.Dialog` names - one of four, 420, 520, 640 or 760, or 800
  for the domain and account dialogs and their many tabs (`ManyTabsWidth`), the IP range and route dialogs starting
  from 640 and widening to their tab strips where the headers need them - and none a number of its own, in its frame's
  call or in a constant, as the IP range and route dialogs' 560 and the domain and account dialogs' 800 were, and a
  page's column the form width, 760, or the overviews', 1000 (`DesignTokens.OverviewWidth`); every card of a settings
  page and of each of its tabs, and of Server sendout, Diagnosing stalled mail, REST API keys and About, ends at the
  form width's edge (`FormColumnPanel`); the dead styles are gone; and `build/check-spacing.py`, which the checkers
  job runs, fails a margin or a padding written off the scale, its baseline the optical nudges and the rest the tree
  held, which may only shrink. `SpacingScaleTests` and `FormColumnTests` hold the tokens, the scaffold, the dialogs'
  widths, in the frame's call and in a constant, the list cards and the pages' columns.

- **Fixed: opening the help pane squeezed the Control Panel's sidebar and cut three group names, Welcome, Dashboard
  and About were letters in the rail, and the breadcrumb could wrap onto two lines.** The sidebar was a star column
  beside the page, so the help pane, a column of fixed width, took its width from both: opened in a 1280-pixel window
  it pushed the tree from 280 pixels to its 200 floor and cut "Accounts & doma...", "Mail flow & deliv..." and
  "Connections & pr..."; and at the window's opening size "Web services & autoconfiguration" was cut in English and
  seven page labels in German. The tree is now a share of the window's width - 310 pixels at 1280 - set in pixels as
  the window changes (`Services/ShellGeometry`), so the pane takes its width from the page alone; where the tree and
  the pane would leave the page less than 512 pixels, the sidebar is the rail while the pane is open, a glyph opening
  its group's pages in the flyout, and the tree again once the pane closes, neither recorded as a choice; a keyboard
  on the tree's row for the page goes to the rail's glyph for it and back, where it was left on the window. At 1280
  the tree holds every English page label whole and five of the seven German ones; "Übersicht der
  Transportverschlüsselung" and "Servergrenzen und Experteneinstellungen" still end in an ellipsis, whole in their
  tool tips. Welcome, the Dashboard and About have glyphs of their own - a house, a chart and an information mark -
  where the rail drew their translated initials and their labels started left of the groups' in the tree, and Sign-in
  & access is a person with a lock, where it was a second shield beside Spam & virus filtering's. The breadcrumb's
  trail no longer wraps: where its line is too short, the groups' segments are cut short first and the page's name
  last, each with an ellipsis and whole in its tool tip, so that beside the help pane in the narrowest window the bar
  still names the page (`Views/Scaffold/BreadcrumbTrailPanel`), and the Related links keep twelve pixels from it,
  where "Certificates (ACME)" went onto a second line at 760 pixels and "Transport security" ran into "Related:"
  (review findings F021, F022, F023, F047; T3.3 work item 7). Beside the wider sidebar the Domains page's alias and
  list cards keep 270 pixels each where they kept 280, so that they stay side by side at 1280, and the audit trail's
  grid scrolls sideways where it had cut its Detail column to a letter, Detail floored at 120 pixels and the columns
  before it at their words. `ShellGeometryTests` holds the widths, the rail beside the pane, the glyphs, the
  breadcrumb and the audit trail's floors.

- **Fixed: the page tour's button and the help pane's were one question-mark glyph, 250 pixels apart.** On a page a
  tour visits - Domains, TCP/IP ports, SSL certificates and the Dashboard - the header's question mark started the
  tour, the command bar's question mark opened the help pane, and Welcome's Show me around was the same glyph again;
  only the tool tips told them apart. The tour's button is now a light bulb with "Show me around" beside it where the
  header has room for the words, and the light bulb alone where only that keeps the page's actions beside its title,
  as the owner decided on 9 October 2026; Welcome's is the light bulb too, and the question mark is the help pane's
  alone. Like the tour's card, the header's button carries no Alt key, since it is on whichever page a tour visits;
  and its accessible name starts with the words it shows in every language, as WCAG 2.5.3 asks, where in eight of them
  the button said the server's tour and its name this page's (review findings F024, F081; T3.3 work item 8).
  `TourGlyphTests` holds the glyphs, the rule for the words and the name in every catalogue.

- **Fixed: the help pane's All documentation could be pressed on its own list, its heading links were too small a
  target, and a search that matched nothing said nothing.** With the list of every document showing, the pane's only
  button was All documentation, which rebuilt the same list; the links to a document's headings were 12-pixel words
  with two pixels above and below, about 20 pixels tall where WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24; and a search term that matched
  nothing left the pane as it was. All documentation is now disabled while the list is what the pane shows - on its
  own and under a page that no guide covers - and enabled again with a document, the keyboard going to the search when
  it was pressed from the keyboard; each heading link is 24 pixels tall at least; and a line under the search box
  says "Match 2 of 5 - press Enter for the next." or "No match for "qqzz" in this document.", which a screen reader
  hears as it changes and which goes with the search whatever the pane shows next, a link to a document this copy does
  not have included (review finding F027; T3.3 work item 9). `HelpPaneControlsTests` holds the three. Two new strings
  in all seventeen languages.

- **Fixed: three small misalignments - the sign-in card's two-factor link, the Domains page's untitled domains card,
  and its domain list scrolling inside a page that scrolls.** The link's words started ten pixels right of the
  card's captions, boxes and Connect, pushed in by the link button's own padding; they start on the card's text
  column now, the hover fill and the focus rectangle still reaching past them inside the card. The domains card had
  no title, so its search sat 23 pixels above the accounts card's beside it; it is titled Domains, and the two
  searches share a line. In the one column of a narrow window the domain list kept a floor of three rows and needed
  a scroll bar of its own for the fourth domain, inside the page's and over the rows' delete buttons; there it shows
  as many rows as it has, up to 25, and the page alone scrolls, and each of the page's four lists keeps its rows
  clear of its own scroll bar while it shows one (review findings F032, F100, F101; T3.3 work item 10).
  `AlignmentFixesTests` holds the three.

- **Fixed: cards and grids that were titled, named or sized out of step with their neighbours - the suppression
  list, the DKIM key rotation, the TCP/IP ports and routes grids, the Welcome page's intents, the setting profiles
  card and the domains' globe.** The suppression list's list card was the page's one untitled card, its two grids
  were not linked, and the list's Why column said "Temporary failure" and "Policy refusal" where the bounce counts
  said "Soft" and "Policy": the card is Suppressed addresses, each grid is named as its card is titled, selecting an
  address selects its row of the counts, which their grid scrolls to while the page stays where it is, the counts'
  columns are named by the list's categories - their address staying in view as they scroll sideways under the longer
  names - the list's two headers are Reason and Status code and the counts' Last status code, the Add dialog says that
  addresses on the server's own domains cannot be added where it read as if the address would be refused mail, and its
  expiry box is 160 pixels where it spanned the dialog. The domain dialog's DKIM rotation buttons were the tab's last
  row, directly above Save and Cancel, and read as one footer with them; they and the rotation's state are on a
  surface of their own. The TCP/IP ports grid's fixed columns totalled 880 pixels and left the certificate's name some
  150 - "mail.example.com (Let..." - while Address took 170 for "0.0.0.0"; they are no wider than their words now,
  SMTP authentication is the column AUTH with its words as the header's tool tip, and the certificate has the rest.
  The routes grid cut German's Retries at 80 pixels and named one column Auth, the group's one abbreviation: every
  column is floored at its header, Authentication is in words, and a route's row says its retries and its sign-in to a
  screen reader; and a header's width is measured as the window draws it, where at 150 % a header of Latin letters
  came out a pixel or two narrower and a column floored at it was cut, as the suppression list's "Last status code"
  was. The Welcome page's intent rows looked like text: each ends in a chevron, says its blurb as its help text, and
  the two grids' right columns end where the notices above them do; the walk's and the sample domain's offers are
  Normal notices where they carried the Information word. The setting profiles card took eight pixels of inset where
  every content card takes the card's own, was an empty rectangle of column headers when the server could not be read,
  and in another language put its translated heading over the server's English: it takes the card's inset, each of its
  columns floored at its header so that the inset does not cut German's "Verlangt eine Bestätigung", says "Nothing to
  compare until the server can be read." or "Choose a profile to compare it with this server." in the table's place,
  and says that the profiles' own words come from the server in English. And the domain rows' globe is the secondary
  text, as the account rows' glyph is, where it spent the brand blue on every row (review findings F318, F320, F322,
  F307, F308, F098; T3.3 work item 11). `CardGridTidyingTests` holds them. Seven new strings in all seventeen
  languages; six that nothing uses any more are gone.

- **Fixed: the sign-in page called a mistyped password Critical, took Enter from every control on it, said nothing to a
  screen reader while it worked and opened on localhost and Administrator every time, and the window never said which
  server it managed.** A password or a one-time code the server refused, and a second-factor prompt cancelled, are now
  a Warning, the reader's to type again; only a server that could not be reached or asked is Critical, where every
  failure was, and that was the first word the page's assertive notice spoke. Enter on a field presses the sign-in
  button as the page's default button, and Enter on the closed Language box opens its list, as F4 does, where a
  KeyDown handler on the whole page started a sign-in from any control that left Enter unhandled, the closed Language
  box among them. The busy line is a polite live region, announced as it changes - "Contacting localhost…", then
  "Signing in…" - and the progress ring is named "Signing in". The server and the user name of the last sign-in that
  worked are kept beside the window's other settings, as `LastHost` and `LastUser` under
  `HKCU\Software\hMailServer\ControlPanel` - never the password - and the page opens on them, localhost and
  Administrator where nothing is kept. Once signed in, the window's title, in its title bar, the taskbar and Alt+Tab,
  is "mail.example.com - hMailServer Control Panel", so that two Control Panels on two servers can be told apart, and
  the product alone again on the sign-in page. Setup, which asks for an open Control Panel to be closed before it
  installs, looked for that window by the title "hMailServer Control Panel" alone, which a signed-in window's title no
  longer is and a Japanese, Swedish, Turkish or Chinese one never was; it now looks for the named mutex the Control
  Panel holds while it runs as well, and still for the title, which finds one from before the mutex.
  `SignInMemoryTests` holds the levels, the prefill, the title, setup's check and the page and the window to using
  them.

- **Fixed: with values it could not read, the setup checklist drew a tally and a next step counted from them above the
  notice that said so, and that notice spoke of "the items above"; and nothing on the tour's card said that F6 reaches
  it.** With the link lost the checklist began "4 need action, 7 cannot be told from here, 0 done, 4 not needed. Next
  step: MTA-STS policy hosting..." and only then "11 values could not be read: ... The items above may be incomplete."
  The notice is now first and says it in the DNS records page's words, "Some values could not be read, so the sections
  below may be incomplete." with the reason last; and while values could not be read the tally begins "An item that
  depends on a value that could not be read is counted as one that cannot be told, unless what was read already shows
  that it needs action.", and neither the tally nor a card names a next step - no card carries the Next step pill or the
  page's primary button, and the Dashboard's attention card, which lists the same steps, marks none of them Next step
  either - since the step it would name is the first of the items that could be told, not the first that needs doing. An
  item that judges a value the checklist could not read says Cannot tell: with the domain list unread, DKIM signing said
  "No domains are configured" as Not needed, ARC sealing, where it is on, that no domain could seal, and MTA-STS policy
  hosting was Done with no domain's record looked up; ARC filtering, on with its sealers named and its DMARC failure
  score unread, was Done; and a server checklist that could not be parsed in full lost the items after the fault, where
  it is now one item that cannot be told, as one that could not be read at all is. The tour never takes the keyboard -
  F6 moves into its card and Escape ends the tour from inside it - and neither the card, its accessible name nor its
  first announcement said so: the card's help text says "Press F6 to reach the tour's buttons; while one of them has the
  keyboard, Escape ends the tour.", and the first step of a run shows the sentence as a tertiary line under its buttons
  and adds it to what is announced; and the card's buttons wrap, where from the second step "Rundgang überspringen" ran
  off the card's right edge in German. `SetupChecklistReadFailureTests`, `TourKeysHintTests` and `TourCardButtonsTests`
  hold them.

- **Fixed: a scanner test that failed without the server's words said only "Connection failed." or "Scanner test
  failed."** Where the server gives no detail, the Anti-spam page's SpamAssassin test now says "SpamAssassin did not
  answer at localhost:783. Check that spamd is running, listens on that port and allows this server
  (--allowed-ips).", the Anti-virus page's ClamAV test "ClamAV did not answer at 127.0.0.1:3310. Check that clamd is
  running and listens on TCP (TCPSocket in clamd.conf).", an IPv6 address in brackets, and its ClamWin test "The
  scanner gave no result. Check the clamscan.exe path and the signature database folder." The server's own words,
  where it gives them, are shown as before. `ScannerTestFallbackTests` holds the three sentences and the page to
  using them.

- **Fixed: Directory synchronisation said a failed read of the server's domain list as Information, with no next
  step.** "Cannot tell from here - the server's domain list could not be read..." was a violet Information notice in
  its readiness card, which understated a read that failed. It is now said at the level of the cause, as the other
  pages say a failed read: Critical when the link to the service was lost, ending "That is a connection problem
  rather than a configuration one: press Reload once the connection is back.", and a Warning when the server
  answered and could not give the list, ending "Press Reload to read it again. Why:" and the server's reason.
  `DirectorySyncDomainReadTests` holds the levels and the sentences.

- **Fixed: the Administrator roles page said a missing address or role in an amber notice under its form, said
  nothing when a role was given or taken away, and nothing on it said where custom roles are made.** "An account
  address is required." and "Choose a role to give." were a Warning notice under the form - the level a lost link
  has - often below the window's edge; they are now said on their boxes, both at once, with the keyboard put in the
  first, and Give the role and Take the role away stay beside the boxes when a message appears. A role given now says
  "helen@example.com now holds helpdesk." and selects the assignment, and a role taken away says that the account no
  longer holds it and holds what its admin level gives it, where the boxes emptied and the list reloaded without a
  word. A new administrator looked for an Add role button: the Roles card says "The built-in roles cannot be changed.
  Custom roles are made over the REST API, and the Control Deck deletes one that nobody holds." with Open the
  Control Deck under it - the Deck lists, gives out and deletes roles and makes none, which the review's proposed
  wording said it did - and REST API keys, whose key holds a role, names Administrator roles among its related pages.
  `RolesFormFeedbackTests` holds the messages, the outcomes, the card and the related pages, and the card's sentence
  to what the Deck's Roles view does.

- **Fixed: in Japanese, the setup checklist's DKIM signing item named the record to publish
  `<selector>.domainkey.<domain>`.** The translation had lost the underscore of `_domainkey`, read as an Alt key and
  moved to the end of the text as "(_D)", so that a reader who published what it said made a record no receiver looks
  up; it now names `<selector>._domainkey.<domain>`, and the "(_D)" is gone. `build/check-catalogues.py` holds every
  translation to the DNS labels its English names - `_domainkey`, `_dmarc`, `_mta-sts`, `_smtp._tls` and the service
  labels - and found no other.

- **Fixed: the Domains & accounts page filled the Address box with "user@" as text, lost the account it had just made
  or moved, could not find an address of another domain, and named no row to a screen reader.** The Address box held
  "user@" and the domain in the primary colour, so an untouched Create account made a mailbox called user and typing a
  name meant selecting "user" first; the other boxes' placeholders read "newdomain.com", "alias@domain",
  "target@anywhere" and "list@domain". The box is now empty with "name@" and the domain as its placeholder, the alias
  and list boxes show "sales@" and "team@" and the domain, the Domain box example.org and the alias's target
  person@example.net, and a name typed without an @ in the account, alias or list box is completed with the selected
  domain. Create account selects and scrolls to the new account, as Add domain does, and a mailbox moved or renamed to
  another domain from its dialog is followed there and selected, where the page read the old domain's accounts again
  and the mailbox vanished. A whole address of another hosted domain in Search accounts selects that domain first,
  where "user01@example.net" found nothing while example.com was selected. On an empty server "Add a domain" is the
  one primary button and Create account a plain one until a domain is selected. Every row button is named for its
  row - "Properties of domain example.com", "Edit account user@example.com", "Delete alias info@example.com" - where a
  screen reader heard "Properties" and "Delete domain" on every row, each name starting with the button's words in
  every language. `HostedAddressTests` holds the completion, the placeholders, the search, the selections, the primary
  button and the names.

- **Fixed: the account dialog's Folders tab was a blank box over "0 folders.", Remove the photo could be pressed with
  no photo, and the distribution list members dialog never said how many members a list has.** The folder list of an
  empty mailbox now says in its place "No folders yet. The server creates INBOX when the mailbox is first opened; Add
  folder creates one now.", after a read that worked and never after one that failed; Remove the photo on the
  Directory entry tab is enabled only while the account has a photo or a new one is chosen, where it was live under
  "This account has no photo."; and the members dialog's heading has the count under it, "3 members" in the language's
  own plural forms, after a read that worked. `AccountDialogStatesTests` holds the empty state, the button and the
  count.

- **Fixed: a blocked domain and a rule switched off showed their state only as a word at the row's end.** On the
  Allowed and blocked domains page a Blocked entry differed from an Allowed one only in its word; the Action cell is
  now led by the status mark, the Critical cross for Blocked and the Normal circle for Allowed, in the level's colour
  by resource key, and the column is floored at either word with its mark and sorts by the word. On the Rules page,
  and the account dialog's Rules tab, a disabled rule differed only by "No" in the Enabled column; its name is now in
  the secondary text, as an inactive domain's is, and the column is a pill, On at the Good level or Off at the Normal
  one. Ctrl+C on a row copies both cells as their words, Allowed or Blocked and On or Off. The empty quarantine's
  glyph was made a neutral inbox by the failed-read work and stays so. `StateMarksTests` holds the mark, the greyed
  name, the pill, what each copies and the glyph.

- **Fixed: timestamps came in several forms and never said whose clock they were read by.** The delivery queue showed
  the server's raw "2026-10-08 02:36:53", the message trace and the suppression list the same form, the audit trail and
  the eDiscovery page Unix times as this computer's local time in that fixed form, the REST API keys "7 January 2027
  10:00", the SSL certificates page, the setting profiles and the DKIM key rotation yyyy-MM-dd whatever the language,
  and the ACME card its day, month and year in one order in every language. Every date now goes through one helper,
  `Services/ServerTimeText`, which the account dialog's last sign-in, Server status's start, the quarantine's held
  times, the allowed and blocked domains' Added and the backup list's dates use as well: the reader's short date and
  time, with "(server time)" in the column's header or after the value and the whole time in a cell's tool tip. In a
  session on the server's own computer the queue says how long ago a message was created ("3 h ago"), and in one from
  another computer the date under "Created (server time)", sorted by the time; when a message is tried again is its
  State's, which took the place of the Next try column (the delivery queue's entry above). The message trace's times are
  under "When (server time)", to the second, and the suppression list's under "Since (server time)", "Expires (server
  time)", "Last bounce (server time)" and "Last delivered (server time)", each column sorted by the time, and the
  server's and each domain's allow and block list says when an entry expires in the reader's short date and time under
  "Expires (server time)", where it wrote the general form with the seconds and named no clock. The audit trail's When
  and the eDiscovery page's Opened and When are in this computer's time with the seconds, headed "(server time)" in a
  session on the server and "(this computer's time)" in one from elsewhere, and sort by the time; the API keys say
  "Expires 07/01/2027 10:00 (server time)." A day in a sentence - a certificate's "Valid until 09/12/2026", the day a
  profile was applied - is the reader's short date, the key rotation's times and when the message store was measured the
  reader's short date and time. `ServerTimeTextTests` holds every form, the pages' use of the helper and that none of
  them writes a date in a form of its own again.

- **Fixed: the Windows Text size setting had no effect on the Control Panel.** Nothing read it, so raising Text size
  to 125 or 150 per cent changed nothing and only display scaling made the text larger. The Control Panel now reads it
  (the registry's `TextScaleFactor`) when it starts, before the first window, and draws its text at it: every
  font-size resource - the type ramp's tokens and WPF-UI's own, the size of every box, button, list and grid - is set
  at the factor, the shared styles, the shell and the sign-in, Domains, Dashboard and Live logs pages take their text
  sizes from those tokens where they wrote numbers, and the sizes pages set in code (`Typography`) are at it too, the
  help pane's headings among them, which kept 20 and 16 pixels and so stood smaller than the text under them; an icon
  keeps its size. Live logs' lines keep their spacing as their text grows, where at 150 per cent the log's 18-pixel
  text stood in lines 17 pixels apart and each line ran into the next. Grid floors are measured in the scaled font, a
  dialog widens with its text within the work area, the one-time code boxes grow with their digits, and no column of
  words keeps a fixed width that larger text cuts short: the certificates grid's Name, Certificate and Private key
  columns, fixed at 170 and 210 pixels, share the width over a floor or keep floors that rise with the text size; the
  allowed and blocked domains' Added, the suppression list's Why, Since, Expires, Last bounce, Last delivered, Last
  status and Listed, the IP ranges' addresses and their SMTP, IMAP and POP3, the incoming relays' addresses and a
  chart's data table's times, fixed at 70 to 170 pixels, are as wide as their words over floors of their widest,
  measured at the text size, where at 150 per cent Added read "9/28/2026 8:18 P…" and the suppression list's dates
  were cut mid-glyph; the lists of fields' named widths rise with the text size, no list's column is narrower than its
  header and none of a named width narrower than its widest tick-box word, number or date; no column of the IP ranges
  or the delivery queue is narrower than its header, Priority, ID and Tries included, columns of numbers that keep
  their pixels, where at 150 per cent German cut "Priori…" and "Vers…"; these floors are whole device pixels, rounded
  up, where at a display scale of 150 per cent a column floored at a word was drawn a third of a pixel narrower and
  cut it; the message trace's addresses end in an ellipsis where they are wider than their share; and the rules grid's
  Enabled column fits its pill. Three WPF-UI styles that held the size their dictionary had when it was read - a
  caption with an Alt key, a list box's rows, a rich text box - take the scaled size. When Windows says the setting
  changed, the resources follow at once and a toast says that pages already open keep the rest of their text at the
  old size until the Control Panel is restarted. docs/ControlPanelDesign.md says the rule. `TextScaleTests` holds the
  factor, the ramp, the start-up, the tokens and line heights on every converted file, the sizes set in code, the grid
  floors, the dialogs and the columns, and that no column of words in a page's XAML or built in code is a fixed number
  of pixels.

- **Fixed: the allow and block lists' Add and Edit refused an entry that never expires, and an expiring one unless its
  date was typed again.** The dialog sent its expiry date whether or not "Stops mattering at a date" was ticked, and
  the server, which reads a date given as text only as yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss, refused the empty box with "ExpiresTime
  must be a date and time written as yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss."; and Edit opened the box on the reader's general form of
  the date the server holds - "12/31/2026 12:00:00 AM", "31.12.2026 00:00:00", or "12/30/1899 12:00:00 AM" for an
  entry that never expires - which the server refused as well, or, in Japanese, read by position and saved with the
  minutes and seconds of a time before ten o'clock wrong: "2026/12/31 9:30:45" as 09:00:05. The box now opens on the
  server's own form, the one its caption names, and empty for an entry that never expires, and the date is sent only
  while the switch is on, an empty one then refused on its field as before. The server's list and each domain's, on
  the domain's dialog, are the same editor. `ListExpiryDialogTests` holds the box's text in four languages, what is
  sent with the switch off and on, and the dialog's use of both.

- **Fixed: the Domains page's rows said Edit and Delete in words beside the lists' glyphs, and the page had no
  Refresh.** The domain rows showed a text Edit beside a glyph delete and the account rows a text Edit and Delete, while
  the alias and distribution-list rows used 24-pixel glyphs - three button styles on one page, against the owner's
  decision 15 (row actions are 24-pixel icon buttons named for their row). Every row action on the page is now a glyph
  in a 24-pixel box (Edit24, Delete24 in the danger text colour), its tool tip and accessible name the act and the row -
  "Edit domain example.com", "Delete account user01@example.com". The page now has Refresh in its header, as every list
  page does (review finding F062), where only F5 read it again; Alt+R is Refresh's here as on every list page (decision
  3), so the account form's Address takes Alt+S and Add list Alt+T, and the captions that met Refresh's key in Swedish,
  Norwegian, Spanish, Finnish, Danish, Ukrainian, French, Italian and Japanese and Chinese take another.
  `DomainsRowTests` holds that every row action is a named 24-pixel glyph, and `NoRowButton_CarriesACaption` and
  `AccessKeysTests` the rest.

- **Fixed: Message trace cut every Status pill to its mark when the delivery queue's Trace message opened it.** The
  Status column was Auto with no floor, and the queue's Trace message fills the grid before the page's first layout, so
  the column kept its header's width and every pill read "■ ." - "OK 250", "Deferred 451" and "Refused 550" gone in
  every language - until a search drew them again. The column is floored at its header and at the widest of the three
  classes' pills in the reader's language, measured as the pill draws it (`GridStyles.PillCellWidth`).
  `MessageTraceStatusTests` holds the floor and the pill's measure against its template.

- **Fixed: the audit trail put what changed off the page at 1280 by 800.** With the interface and the address as
  columns, and the columns of words floored at their widest word up to 180 pixels, the grid was 1248 pixels wide in a
  view of 877 in English (1215 in German, 1223 in Japanese): it scrolled sideways on opening, the action was cut at the
  view's edge ("Aktualis") and Detail - what changed, the column a reader comes for - was entirely off screen, where
  after Tier 1 every column was on the page. The interface and the address the change came over are now the selected
  row's, on lines of their own in the strip under the list beside what changed ("Interface: Control Panel", "IP address:
  10.1.0.42"), and the four columns of words are floored at their widest word up to 120 pixels, a longer one ending in
  an ellipsis and whole in its tool tip and the strip: the time, Who, Object, Name, Action and Detail's 200 fit the
  view. `AuditTrailPageTests` holds the columns, the floor and the strip's lines.

- **Fixed: the Suppression list's bounce counts scrolled 317 pixels past their card at 1280 by 800.** Under the category
  names the list's Reason column uses and the "(server time)" headers of its two dates, the counts' grid was 1208 pixels
  wide in a view of 891 in English (559 pixels too wide in German, 332 in Japanese), its last bounce and last delivery
  off screen on opening, where after Tier 1 it scrolled 125. The last status code, the last bounce and the last delivery
  are now the selected address's, in a strip under the counts titled by the address, the dates in the reader's form and
  marked as the server's ("Last bounce: 10/12/2026 9:11 PM (server time)"); and each count's header wraps onto two lines
  where it is two words, the column as wide as the header's widest word, so that "Harte Unzustellbarkeit" no longer
  makes a column of one digit 160 pixels wide. The counts fit their card at 1280 in English, German and Japanese and
  keep the categories' one name in both grids (review finding F318). `SuppressionListPageTests` holds the columns, the
  wrapping headers and the strip.

- **Fixed: five dates were still the server's own text, against the reader's culture.** The Updates page said "6.3.7 is
  available (published 2026-10-01)" and "This is the latest release, checked 2026-10-12 08:00:00"; Diagnostics' message
  store card "Last scan: 2026-10-05 21:39:37."; the setup checklist "The Small office profile was applied on
  2026-10-01."; the update install "recorded in the Sigstore log at 2026-10-10T09:12:00Z"; and the Auto-ban page's
  never-ban names an Added column of "2026-09-01 10:12:00" under a header that named no clock - where the owner's
  decision 13 asks for the reader's culture and "(server time)", and ISO only in text that describes a format. The
  feed's day and the checklist's days are the reader's short date, the last check and the last scan the reader's short
  date and time marked as the server's, the Sigstore log's time the reader's short date and time marked UTC, and the
  never-ban names' column "Added (server time)", sorted by the time. A text in another form is shown as it came.
  `ServerTimeTextTests` holds each; `FirstHourDays` says which first-hour texts carry a day.

- **Fixed: a settings page that could not read its settings offered no Try again.** Every list page's failed read says
  so at Critical with a Try again button (review finding F179), but the server settings pages' notice that settings
  could not be read, and the feature pages' notice that their values are hMailServer.ini's because the server did not
  answer, had none: the reader had to find Reload in the header. Both notices now carry the same Try again, which reads
  the page again as Reload does, kept from one failure to the next so that the keyboard stays on it
  (`ReadFailure.TryAgainOn`). `FailureStateTests` holds both pages.

- **Fixed: eDiscovery told a signed-in administrator to sign in.** With a session that holds no password the REST API
  can sign in with, the page said "Sign in to a server first." as a Warning under the shell's Connected pill - the
  defect review finding F217 put right on the settings pages, on a page outside its list. The page now says what the
  settings pages say: that the session holds no password the REST API can sign in with, and to sign in again with the
  administrator's user name and password. Only a page with no session at all says "Sign in to a server first.".
  `FailureStateTests` holds it.

- **Fixed: placeholders that read as values already set.** A placeholder is an example of what the box takes, marked as
  one - "e.g. mail.example.com" - and never the field's name, its default or what an empty box means (review findings
  F138 and F303), but some forty boxes showed a bare example or their default: the Updates page's Unattended window "Sun
  03:00" under "empty = never apply on its own", which read as a schedule in force, and its feed URL box the real feed's
  address; Directory authentication's Port "Automatic - 636 for LDAPS, 389 otherwise", cut at its box's edge, and its
  Timeout "10"; Directory synchronisation's five attribute and number boxes their defaults; the settings pages' hosts,
  addresses, folders and URLs bare; and sentences - "Falls back to the ACME certificate", "Leave both empty for plain
  HTTP", "Optional", "your application / client ID" - in boxes whose caption or hint should say them. Every example is
  now marked, by the box where a settings row holds it (`ExamplePlaceholder.Shown`); a default or what an empty box
  means is the caption's or the hint's, two of them new hints in all 17 languages ("Left empty, the ACME certificate is
  used.", "Left empty, the key may act on every domain.") and the OAuth2 audience a hint of its own; and the sign-in
  card's server box, whose placeholder repeated its caption, shows an example. On the Domains page the alias form's
  Delivers to and the list form's address are as wide as their half card, their button under them at the right edge,
  where beside the button the boxes were about 120 pixels at 1280 and their examples read "person@examp" and
  "team@example.". `PlaceholderExamplesTests` holds every placeholder a view writes to a marked example or one of a few
  kinds named with their reason.

- **Fixed: Setting profiles said a failure as a fact, and its table showed four of its five rows.** The notice that a
  profile could not be applied, in full or at all, and that a way back is held and cannot be read, was drawn at
  Information like every other state of what is applied; it is a Warning now, and the rest stay Information. And the
  caption that the profiles' own words come from the server in English sat above the comparison table, taking one of the
  five rows it showed at 1280 by 800 in Japanese; it ends the line of the steps' heading, "What it cannot do for you",
  in the caption's size, and is a caption of its own under the table only for a profile with no steps.
  `ProfilesPageFlowTests` and `CardGridTidyingTests` hold both.

- **Fixed: the delivery queue's ID column was right-aligned as a count.** Review finding F248 asked for the ID narrow
  and left-aligned, and the page's own comment said so, but the column carried the number styles - given to it so that
  it passed the rule against columns of words at a fixed width - and its IDs and header sat at the right. It is as wide
  as its widest ID over a floor of 56 pixels, left-aligned. `DeliveryQueueTests` holds it.

- **Fixed: Allow or block a domain cut its Action option in German.** At the default dialog width the option
  "Zugelassen: kein Greylisting, keine Abweisung wegen der Spam-Bewertung" read "... wegen der Spam-Bew", and Polish,

- **Fixed: DNS records' captions ended in colons.** A caption names its field and ends in no colon (review findings F043
  and F301), but five on the DNS records page still did - "Report mailbox:" and "TXT value:" the very examples F301

- **Fixed: six Japanese texts wrote a full-width colon.** The Japanese catalogue writes a colon half-width with a space

- **Fixed: the sidebar's rows ran under its scroll bar.** The scroll bar is drawn over the rows, and since the

- **Fixed: list toolbars wrapped their actions a word at a time beside the search.** A list page's actions stayed beside
  its search and filters while the widest of them fitted there, and wrapped there: at 760 pixels the IP ranges'

- **Fixed: search placeholders cut at the box's edge.** A list's search box is at most 360 pixels, and its placeholder

  и блокировок". `SearchPlaceholderFitTests` holds every search placeholder in every language to its box.

- **Fixed: the Rules page's THEN footer wrapped its Primary onto a second line at 1280.** With Up and Down beside its
  three captioned buttons the half-width card's footer needed more than the card had once the sidebar was wider, and Add
  action, the Primary, sat alone on a second line in English, German and Japanese; in German the IF footer wrapped its
  Add criterion the same way. Up and Down are a column of two glyphs beside the list of actions they reorder, named for

  buttons would not fit their card on one line, not only below 340 pixels. `RulesPageTests` and `RulesActionOrderTests`
  hold both.

- **Fixed: 34 texts were pieces of a sentence that the reason for a failure was glued to.** "Could not read the list: ",
  "Could not read the domains: ", "The run failed: ", "Could not copy: ", "Scope: " and 29 more ended in a colon and a
  space, and the page put the reason after them, so no language could put the reason anywhere else (review finding F283,

  {0}" - the same words in each language where they were, ready for a translator to reorder; the two labels set before a

  text with white space at either edge.

- **Fixed: hints of three to five sentences on the settings pages, and INI keys inside hints.** The owner's decision 11
  asks for two sentences of hint on the page - what a setting does, and its safe value or what follows from it - with
  the rest in the help, and an INI key name only as a small caption; it was carried out on the Anti-spam and Anti-virus
  settings pages alone. Seventy hints on Protocols, Delivery of e-mail, SSL/TLS, Auto-ban, Logging, Performance,
  Advanced, Webmail, Administrative access, Transport security, API & monitoring, Updates, Server limits & expert
  settings, DNS resolver, Web services & autoconfiguration, Backup & restore, a distribution list's dialog, Directory
  authentication and Directory synchronisation ran to three, four and five, and Directory authentication ended each of
  its hints with "Stored as [LDAP] Port." Each hint keeps the two of its sentences that say what the setting does and
  its safe value or consequence, the same two in every language; the sentences it loses are in the new
  docs/SettingsReasons.md, under the page and the setting's caption, which the help now opens for the nine pages no
  other document was about; and Directory authentication names each key in the small line under its editor. Seven
  hints the settings pages take from the notes pinned to their settings - bounce processing, what happens to a listed
  recipient, reading delivery reports, syslog, the worker thread priority, the four cache sizes and the OpenTelemetry
  traces endpoint - ran to three as well, and keep two the same way. `SettingsHintLengthTests` holds every hint on
  those pages and every such note to two sentences, the keys to the small line, and the reasons to the document.

- **Fixed: the Levels tab of the domain and account dialogs was headed by the server's own keys.** Each setting a
  domain or an account may hold its own value of was headed "max_message_size_kb", "session_idle_seconds",
  "quota_grace_percent" and so on, in mono type and in every language, against the owner's decision 11 (a key name
  only as a small caption). Each is headed by its name as the page or tab that edits it for the server or the domain
  says it - "Maximum message size (KB)", "Seconds a session may go unused" - in every language, with the key beside it
  as a small caption in the tertiary colour, and in its tool tip, for the REST API that sets a level by it; a refusal
  at the save names the setting the same way. `SettingLevelsTests` holds a name for every setting the server has
  levels for.

- **Fixed: the Japanese and Chinese audit trail said "time of creation" for an object made.** "Created" is the audit
  trail's Action for a new object and an eDiscovery case's state, and the two catalogues wrote it as the time of
  creation, 作成日時 and 创建时间, beside 更新 and 削除. They say 作成 and 已创建 now; `JapaneseStyleTests` holds both.

- **Changed: the sidebar has a Compliance group and a Virus scanning group, and the spam group is Spam filtering.**
  Monitoring & troubleshooting asks whether mail is flowing, and its last rows were the audit trail, journaling and
  eDiscovery, which answer a compliance question: who changed what, where copies of the mail go and what is held for a
